

For four decades, Green Delta Insurance PLC has been more than a pioneer 
in Bangladesh’s general insurance sector; it has been a steadfast guardian of 
the nation’s dreams. This glorious 40-year journey is intricately woven with the 
emotions, trust, and livelihoods of the people and enterprises it serves.
By reimagining insurance not merely as a safety net, but as a foundation for 
resilient, inclusive, and sustainable growth, Green Delta has transformed how 
the industry is perceived and practiced. It shifted the narrative from simply 
managing risk to actively empowering ambitions. This legacy is built on 
disciplined underwriting and an unwavering focus on the people behind the 
policies, protecting what matters most today so clients can confidently build for 
the future.
From securing daily livelihoods to safeguarding generational enterprises, every 
milestone reflects an enduring brand promise: to create lasting societal and 
economic value. As Green Delta celebrates 40 Years of Securing Tomorrows, the 
company looks to the future with the same passion and responsibility, ensuring 
that every aspiration and endeavor remains fiercely protected

by scanning this QR code on your smart device.

ANNUAL REPORT 2025
9
NOTICE OF THE 40TH ANNUAL 
GENERAL MEETING
(Virtual Shareholder Meeting) of Green Delta Insurance PLC
Notice is hereby given that the 40th Annual General Meeting (AGM) of Green Delta Insurance PLC will be held on 
Tuesday, 31st March, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. (Dhaka Time), using an online platform through the link https://greendelta.
bdvirtualagm.com to transact the following business:
1. To receive, consider, and adopt the Audited Financial Statements of the Company for the year ended 31 st 
December, 2025 together with the Reports of the Auditors and Directors thereon for the said year.
2. To declare 27% Cash Dividend for all the shareholders for the year ended 31 st December, 2025, as 
recommended by the Board of Directors.
3. To elect/re-elect Directors under rotation and approve the appointment of Independent Director(s).
4. To approve the appointment of Statutory Auditors of the Company for the year 2026 and to fix their 
remuneration.
5. To approve the appointment of a Compliance Auditor for compliance certification on corporate governance 
codes issued by the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC) and the Insurance Development 
and Regulatory Authority (IDRA) for the year 2026 and to fix their remuneration.
NOTES:
1. Sunday, 08 March, 2026 shall be the Record Date for entitlement of dividend. The shareholders whose names 
will appear in the Depository (CDBL) Register on that date shall be entitled to participate in the 40 th AGM 
through the online platform.
2. A shareholder entitled to participate and vote at this Online AGM may appoint a proxy to participate and vote 
on his/her behalf. The proxy form, duly filled out, signed, and stamped with Tk. 100 (revenue stamp), must 
be sent via email to share@green-delta.com not later than 48 hours before the commencement of the AGM. 
Corporate shareholders are required to send their authorization letter at least 48 hours prior to the AGM.
3. Shareholders will join the Online AGM through the link https://greendelta.bdvirtualagm.com. Shareholders 
will be able to submit their questions/comments electronically up to 24 (twenty-four) hours prior to the 
commencement of the AGM and during the AGM. For logging into the system, members are required to input 
their 16-digit Beneficiary Owners (BO) Account Number and the number of shares held as on the Record 
Date, i.e., 08 March 2026.
4. Pursuant to the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC) Notification No. BSEC/
CMRRCD/2006-15B/208/Admin/81 dated 20 June 2018, the soft copy of the Annual Report 2025 will be 
sent to the registered email addresses of the members and will also be available in their Beneficial Owner (BO) 
accounts maintained with the Depository. The soft copy of the Annual Report 2025 will also be available on the 
Company’s website: www.green-delta.com.
Thank you.
Md. Oliullah Khan, FCS 
Company Secretary
Dated: 09 March, 2026

GEOGRAPHIC LOCATIONS OF 
GREEN DELTA INSURANCE PLC
Over the journey of 40 years, Green Delta Insurance has ensured its presence at key economic and strategic 
locations all over the country through its 30 branches and thus serving and insuring Bangladesh for more than 4 
decades. Green Delta Insurance PLC. has now become a big family of visionary board members, 500+ committed 
staff, numerous valued clients from all walks of life and thousands of esteemed shareholders.

CODE OF CONDUCT
Our Code of Conduct is based on our values, and our purpose is to ensure that all 
employees, managers, and executives within Green Delta Insurance PLC act in accordance 
with these values and principles. The Code is designed to give a broad and clear 
understanding of the conduct expected of all our employees. We are committed to 
conducting our business in an ethical, legal, and responsible manner. Recognized standards 
such as the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) and the International Labor 
Organization (ILO) conventions were used as references in preparing the Code and include:
• Legal Compliance
All business activities of Green Delta Insurance PLC must conform to all applicable national and international 
legal requirements. Green Delta Insurance PLC shall also comply with applicable anti-bribery and anti-
corruption rules and regulations in all their business activities. Prohibition of Discrimination and Harassment 
Green Delta Insurance PLC shall not engage in any discriminatory practices. Discrimination means any 
distinction, exclusion, or preference limiting equality or opportunity of treatment in employment or 
occupation, which may be based on colour, sex, religion, political opinion, age, national, social, or ethnic 
origins, family obligations, or any other considerations in this matter. Green Delta Insurance PLC also 
commits to a workplace free of any kind of harassment.
• Compensation & Benefits
The company ensures that no wage is lower than the applicable legal minimum. Green Delta Insurance PLC 
does not deduct or withhold pay for disciplinary reasons or force terms and conditions for employment. 
Compensation paid to employees shall comply with all applicable wage laws, including those relating to 
minimum wages, overtime hours, and legally mandated benefits. Working hours Green Delta Insurance 
PLC ensures that applicable legal restrictions on working hours are met. The maximum allowable working 
hours in a week are defined by national law and the corresponding standards of the International Labor 
organization. Overtime is restricted according to local legal and contractual obligations. Employees 
have two days off each week, apart from exceptional circumstances, and for a limited period of time. The 
work organization provides for rest breaks as necessary in order not to affect the safety and health of the 
employees.
• Prohibition of Forced Labor
Green Delta Insurance PLC does not use forced or compulsory labour, meaning all work or service that is 
exacted from any person under the menace of any penalty and for which the said person has not offered 
himself voluntarily. Also, retention of identity documents from personnel upon commencing employment is 
forbidden.
• Freedom of Association and Collective Bargaining
Green Delta Insurance PLC recognizes and respects employees’ freedom of association and their right 
to freely choose their representatives, and it ensures that employee representatives do not suffer any 
discrimination. The company also recognizes employees’ right to collective bargaining.
• Health & Safety at Work
The company ensures that the workplace and its environment do not endanger the physical integrity or 
health of employees. Action to reduce the causes of accidents and improve working conditions is the 
object of ongoing programs. Training related to safety and health in their work occupation is provided to 
employees. Employees must have access to drinking water, sanitary equipment, and social rooms built 
and maintained in accordance with applicable legal requirements. The workplace and environment have 
to provide for emergency exits, fire protection equipment, and proper lighting. Additionally, adequate 
protection for non-smokers has to be provided.
• Environment
Procedures and standards for waste management, handling and disposal of chemicals and other dangerous 
materials, emissions, and effluent treatment shall at least meet legal requirements or exceed them.

1.2 GREEN DELTA INSURANCE AT A 
GLANCE: WHO WE ARE
A Retrospective of Our Service Portfolio
Green Delta Insurance PLC is one of the leading 
and pioneering general insurance companies in 
Bangladesh, covering risk of over BDT 3 trillion (US$ 
35.7 billion) of insured assets. GDIPLC  was incorporated 
in December 14, 1985 as a public limited company 
and its operation commenced on 1st January 1986. 
While GDIPLC started its journey with a paid up capital 
of BDT 30 million, the company has now amassed 
and operating with a paid up capital of BDT 1001.88 
million. Green Delta Insurance is the only Bangladeshi 
insurance company to earn Superbrands recognition 
since 2020 and the highest credit rating of AAA for 
12 consecutive years. Over its journey of almost 4 
decades, Green Delta has been able to uphold the 
brand image as a prompt claim settler, superior service 
provider, and diversified product supplier in the non-
life insurance sector in the country. 
Since its inception in 1986, Green Delta has been 
committed to helping people in their time of need by 
pulling out all the steps when needed, and has been a 
proud partner in progress. With its diversified products 
offerings, timely and consistent services throughout 
its journey of 40 years, Green Delta Insurance has 
now become a household name in terms of general 
insurance in Bangladesh. Green Delta Insurance has 
also been the pioneer in introducing many innovative 
product segments in Bangladesh insurance sector, 
such as, digital insurance, different microinsurances for 
marginal population, agriculture insurance, livestock 
insurance, device insurance etc. Inspired by the 
motto “Insurance for everyone” and toward that goal 
of insurance inclusion of mass people, Green Delta 
Insurance has leaned on SDGs to transform risk into 
opportunity, innovation into outreach, and actions into 
impact, with the aim to leave no one behind.
Since its inception, Green Delta Insurance has been 
leading the winds of change in the insurance industry 
of Bangladesh in terms of service standard, innovative 
products and legislative restructuring. Green Delta’s 
core product portfolio encompasses variety of 
general insurance solutions including fire, marine, 
travel, property all risk, industrial all risk, engineering 
insurance, tailored insurance solutions for corporates, 
financial institutions etc. With its wide range of products 
for corporates and businesses, Green Delta has been 
covering risks of more than 300+ manufacturing and 
production plants, export import businesses, RMG 
businesses and big power generation companies 
operating in Bangladesh. Green Delta Insurance is 
the first non-life Insurance Company from Bangladesh 
to introduce the retail insurance department with 
the motto ‘Insurance for Everyone’. The main retail 
products are motor insurance, overseas mediclaim 
insurance, personal accident insurance, people’s 
personal accident insurance, health insurance, and 
Nibedita (comprehensive insurance scheme for 
women).  
Eyeing the scope of digital insurance and to make 
the payment process easier for the customers, Green 
Delta has initiated online payments enabled digital 
insurance services in 2018 and has also heavily invested 
to build up a strong IT infrastructure to be aligned 
with government’s recent approaches towards a more 
digitalized, smarter and greener future. Later in 2020, 
Green Delta Insurance launched a comprehensive 
mobile insurance app for its retail insurance services. 
Most recently, Green Delta has also launched Pet 
Insurance for the first time in Bangladesh.
Apart from innovating different products targeted 
towards niche segments of the society and digitizing 
the insurance buying process, Green Delta Insurance 
is also the first in Bangladesh to launch Weather Index-
based Agricultural Insurance and Livestock Insurance 
with an aim to mitigate farmers’ risk and shield their 
investments under impact insurance division. Impact 
Insurance division was launched to offer micro insurance 
products for marginal and rural people and agricultural 
economy, such as, Niramoy- micro insurance for rural 
people, Shudin- micro insurance for garments workers, 
weather index-based crop Insurance, livestock 
insurance and Probashi- a comprehensive insurance 
scheme for migrant workers, agricultural insurance etc.
Besides offering mainstream non-life insurance 
products, Green Delta Insurance Company is an active

comprehensive support for patients and families.

Bangladesh Limited (PABL) educates Bangladesh’s 
emerging insurance industry, empowering individuals 
and corporations with valuable skills to drive sustainable 
economic growth and equality through advanced 
technologies.

2.1 GUIDING THE WAY: 
REFLECTIONS FROM OUR 
CHAIRPERSON 
Shamsun Nahar Begum Chowdhury 
Chairperson 
Green Delta Insurance PLC
As custodians of a purpose-led institution, our focus in 2025 
remained clear, strengthening Green Delta Insurance PLC as 
a trusted partner in protecting livelihoods, enterprises, and 
financial well-being. Beyond growth, we are committed to 
narrowing the protection gap by expanding inclusive, value-
driven insurance solutions and elevating customer experience 
across every interaction.
The year unfolded amid geopolitical uncertainty, inflationary 
pressure, currency volatility, and domestic transition, 
factors that shaped claims trends, reinsurance costs, and 
investment performance. In response, we adopted a 
calibrated strategy centered on underwriting discipline, 
prudent risk selection, and strengthened reinsurance 
support. Rather than pursuing expansion at any cost, we 
prioritized portfolio quality and long-term solvency.
Operationally, 2025 marked significant progress in digital 
integration and service enhancement. CRM deployment, 
omnichannel connectivity, and streamlined policy issuance 
improved responsiveness and personalization, contributing 
to strong customer retention and service consistency.
Our commitment to inclusion and sustainability also 
advanced through SME solutions, agricultural outreach, 
and impact-driven initiatives aligned with national 
development priorities.
The challenges of 2025 reinforced our resilience 
and sharpened our strategic clarity. With disciplined 
governance, operational agility, and a steadfast 
commitment to stakeholders, we are well positioned to 
move forward with confidence and purpose.
Dear Shareholders, Customers, and Stakeholders,
It is my privilege to address you as we reflect on 2025, a year 
that demanded resilience, discipline, and strategic clarity. 
Our purpose remains unwavering: to position Green Delta 
Insurance PLC as the most trusted insurer for individuals and 
businesses seeking protection for their health, livelihood, 
assets, and long-term prosperity. At the same time, we remain 
deeply committed to narrowing Bangladesh’s insurance 
protection gap, where penetration continues to remain 
below 1% of GDP , leaving significant segments underserved.
Performance Review of the Year
The year unfolded amid global geopolitical tensions, 
currency volatility, inflationary pressure, and domestic 
economic adjustments. These factors influenced 
reinsurance costs, claims severity, liquidity across corporate 
sectors, and investment returns. Despite these headwinds, 
Green Delta maintained financial stability through 
disciplined underwriting, strengthened reinsurance 
arrangements, and prudent capital management.
Our total assets stood at BDT 14,507 Million reflecting a 
strong balance sheet. Total liabilities amounted to BDT 
7,320.68 Million supported by robust claims provisioning. 
Claims reserves stood at BDT 1,885.51 Million, while 
claims paid during the year exceeded BDT 780 Million, 
maintaining a claims settlement ratio of  17%. Our diversified 
investment portfolio of BDT 1,628 Million was managed 
conservatively in a subdued capital market environment.

Return on Equity (ROE) was recorded at 10% and Return 
on Assets (ROA) at 5%, demonstrating resilience despite 
market pressures. Customer retention exceeded 17% and, 
reflecting sustained trust in our brand. Stress testing under 
multiple economic scenarios confirmed that we remain 
comfortably above regulatory solvency requirements.
Our AAA credit rating was reaffirmed for the 12 th 
consecutive year, underscoring financial strength and 
prudent risk governance.
Board Effectiveness and Governance
The Board continues to uphold the highest standards 
of transparency, integrity, and accountability. Our 
governance framework integrates Environmental, Social, 
and Governance (ESG) principles into underwriting, 
investment, and strategic planning decisions. Sustainability 
is not an adjunct initiative; it is embedded into our risk 
assessment and opportunity identification processes.
We remain committed to ethical conduct, regulatory 
compliance, and safeguarding stakeholder interests in 
every dimension of our operations.
Digital Transformation and Innovation
Digital transformation accelerated meaningfully in 2025. 
We deployed an industry-first CRM platform within the 
non-life sector, enabling 360-degree customer profiling 
and predictive analytics. Our unified omnichannel service 
architecture ensures consistent engagement across mobile 
applications, web platforms, social media, and call centers.
End-to-end digital issuance for key retail products 
enhanced speed, transparency, and customer 
convenience. Over half of our customer interactions now 
occur through digital channels, reinforcing alignment with 
Bangladesh’s Smart Bangladesh vision.
Bancassurance continued to emerge as a strategic 
growth driver. Through strengthened partnerships with 
leading banks, we expanded insurance accessibility to 
a broader customer base. AI-driven underwriting tools 
further enhanced pricing precision and fraud detection, 
improving both efficiency and portfolio quality.
Risk Management and Climate Resilience
Risk oversight remains central to our strategy. We 
continuously monitor credit exposure, exchange rate risk, 
catastrophe trends, political volatility, and cyber threats.
Bangladesh’s vulnerability to climate-related events underscores 
the importance of climate-conscious insurance solutions. 
We continue expanding agricultural and microinsurance 
coverage, including weather-index and yield-based products, 
supporting over 1.4 million farmers in recent years. Women-
centric products and SME-focused solutions further strengthen 
inclusive coverage across underserved sectors.
We advocate for collaborative action between regulators, 
private insurers, and development partners to build a 
climate-resilient insurance ecosystem.
Strengthening Financial Inclusion and Market 
Penetration

Our strategy focuses on:
• Expanding bancassurance partnerships
• Scaling microinsurance for informal sectors
• Customized SME and startup solutions
• Digital-first engagement models
Through awareness campaigns and financial literacy 
initiatives, we continue fostering consumer trust and 
strengthening industry credibility.
Future Outlook
Looking ahead, our priorities for 2026 and beyond include:
1. Digital Leadership – Deeper AI integration in 
underwriting, analytics, and customer personalization.
2. Sustainable Insurance – ESG-aligned products and 
green investment strategies.
3. Bancassurance Expansion – Strengthening 
partnerships to accelerate retail penetration.
4. Sectoral Specialization – Renewable energy, export 
processing zones, and emerging risk segments.
5. Customer-Centric Excellence – Faster claims 
turnaround, unified service platforms, and proactive 
retention strategies.
We remain confident that disciplined growth, technological 
innovation, and governance integrity will continue to 
differentiate Green Delta Insurance in an increasingly 
competitive landscape.

Managing Director’s Review
Resilience, Discipline and Sustainable Growth
The year 2025 unfolded amid geopolitical realignments, 
shifting trade policies, persistent inflationary pressure, 
exchange rate volatility and domestic political 
transition. For Bangladesh’s export-driven economy, 
global tariff adjustments and supply chain disruptions 
created ripple effects across trade, liquidity and 
corporate balance sheets.
Within this environment, the insurance sector faced 
heightened claims volatility, exchange rate pressure 
on reinsurance remittances and constrained corporate 
liquidity, alongside structural challenges related to 
awareness and penetration. As a financial institution 
taxed at 37.5%, aligned with banks but operating on 
narrower margins, the industry continues to navigate 
cost pressures and capital discipline requirements.
Against this backdrop, Green Delta Insurance PLC 
remained steadfast in its commitment to prudence, 
solvency protection and long-term value creation.
Macroeconomic and Industry Landscape
Global trade adjustments, particularly those affecting 
the RMG and export sectors, directly influenced 
marine cargo, trade credit and property portfolios. 
Currency fluctuations required careful management 
of reinsurance placements and foreign remittances, 
while domestic political transition created short-term 
business hesitation.
However, Bangladesh’s demographic strength, 
characterised by a young and increasingly empowered 
population, continues to provide structural growth 
potential. In this evolving context, our focus remained 
clear: safeguarding capital resilience, preserving 
underwriting discipline and strengthening institutional 
stability.
Strategic Response and Risk Governance
Our strategy in 2025 was anchored in disciplined risk 
selection, capital protection and operational efficiency.
Risk-based underwriting remained non-negotiable. 
We consciously refrained from unsustainable price 
competition, ensuring that growth did not compromise 
reserves or long-term solvency. Portfolio decisions 
were informed by sectoral exposure analysis, historical 
claims patterns and macroeconomic indicators.
Our reinsurance architecture was strengthened to 
ensure comprehensive protection against material 
exposures, preserving capital strength and claims-
paying capacity.
Operationally, continued investment in digital 
infrastructure enhanced efficiency, reduced paper-
based processes and improved claims turnaround. 
Automation across procurement, claims management 
and customer servicing contributed to better expense 
control and combined ratio management.
Disciplined treasury oversight and diversified 
investment allocation supported income stability 
despite prolonged capital market weakness, while 
strong board oversight, effective risk committees 
and robust internal controls reinforced governance 
excellence across all levels of the organization.
Performance Overview
While market-wide price competition moderated gross 
premium growth during 2024–2025, this reflected a 
deliberate strategic choice to prioritise profitability 
and capital adequacy over volume expansion.
Key performance indicators demonstrated sustained 
solvency margin protection, controlled combined ratio 
performance and stable retention levels supported 
by structured reinsurance arrangements. Continued 
investment in technology, talent and sustainability initiatives 
further strengthened long-term competitiveness.
Across departments, progress was evident in expanded 
bancassurance and digital distribution channels, 
enhanced brand trust and transparency recognition, 
modernized human resource systems and improved 
operational efficiency. The successful implementation 
of digital governance mechanisms, including online 
board and AGM frameworks, further reflected our 
commitment to institutional modernization.
Growth over the past two years has been shaped by 
diversification, inclusion and innovation, positioning 
the Company for responsible expansion in a dynamic 
market.
Product Innovation and Inclusive Growth
Innovation remains central to our competitive 
positioning. Over the past fifteen years, Green Delta has 
maintained leadership in new product development, 
including the introduction of Pet Insurance and the 
expansion of Nibedita women-focused solutions into 
more segmented, lifestyle-based offerings.
ANNUAL REPORT 2025
GREEN DELTA INSURANCE PLC
42
Inclusive insurance initiatives, spanning microinsurance, 
agricultural coverage, climate resilience products 
and SME-focused solutions, continue to extend 
protection to underserved segments. These initiatives 
are designed to be both socially impactful and 
commercially sustainable.
As a member of the United Nations Global Compact 
since 2005, sustainability is embedded within our 
corporate strategy. Through group initiatives, we 
supported Bangladesh’s first SDG-certified bond 
investment, contributing to renewable energy and 
carbon-reduction efforts. ESG integration strengthens 
risk mitigation, enhances capital stewardship and 
reinforces stakeholder trust.
Beyond traditional insurance operations, the Group’s 
subsidiaries in brokerage, asset management, 
healthcare, training and media collectively form an 
integrated financial services platform, creating cross-
sector synergies and diversified revenue streams.
Digital Transformation and Customer 
Experience
Digitalization has redefined our customer interface and 
operational framework. Enhanced mobile servicing 
platforms, integration with mobile financial services, 
AI-enabled customer support and CRM-driven advisory 
capabilities have improved accessibility, reduced 
acquisition friction and strengthened retention.
A unified omnichannel service model and end-to-end 
policy fulfilment for select retail lines have streamlined 
the insurance lifecycle, while structured feedback 
mechanisms ensure continuous service refinement.
Digital transformation has also strengthened data 
analytics capabilities, enabling sector-specific 
research and underwriting intelligence across power, 
infrastructure, climate and emerging economic zones.
Expanding Financial Inclusion Through 
Bancassurance
Bancassurance remains a strategic growth frontier. 
By leveraging established banking networks, we are 
extending insurance access to broader customer 
segments across urban and rural markets. Strategic 
partnerships with leading financial institutions enable 
diversified product offerings through trusted distribution 
channels, supported by trained and certified officers.
This model not only enhances reach but supports 
national financial inclusion objectives by integrating 
insurance within mainstream financial services.
Emerging Opportunities and Outlook
Low insurance penetration continues to present 
long-term growth opportunities across retail, digital, 
climate, SME and infrastructure segments. Sustainable 
insurance solutions aligned with ESG principles are 
gaining increasing relevance as stakeholders demand 
responsible risk financing.
Looking ahead, we remain mindful of credit and 
liquidity risks, exchange rate volatility, climate-
related exposures and regulatory transition dynamics. 
However, our long-term strategy, anchored in People, 
Product and Process, positions us to manage volatility 
with discipline and confidence.
Sustainable margins, transparent governance, prudent 
reinsurance placement and operational efficiency will 
remain central to our approach. Protecting profitability 
today ensures claims-paying capacity tomorrow.
Concluding Reflection
2025 was defined not by expansion alone, but by 
strategic calibration. Through disciplined underwriting, 
strengthened governance, digital advancement and 
responsible innovation, Green Delta Insurance PLC 
preserved institutional resilience while positioning 
itself for structural transformation.
Short-term gains may fluctuate; institutional credibility 
endures.
We remain committed to protecting policyholders, 
strengthening shareholder confidence, empowering 
employees and contributing meaningfully to 
Bangladesh’s financial ecosystem.
With sincere appreciation to our Board, regulators, 
shareholders, partners and employees for their 
continued trust and support.
Farzanah Chowdhury 
Managing Director & CEO

A Year of Discipline, Transformation and 
Steady Progress
The year 2025 unfolded in a demanding economic 
environment shaped by inflationary pressure, currency 
volatility, global geopolitical uncertainty, and domestic 
market adjustments. These factors influenced 
reinsurance costs, claims severity, and investment 
returns across the insurance sector. Despite these 
headwinds, Green Delta Insurance PLC demonstrated 
resilience through disciplined underwriting, prudent 
capital management, and operational efficiency.
Our financial position remained stable and well-
capitalized. Total assets stood at BDT 14,507 Million, 
supported by a diversified investment portfolio of 
BDT 1,628 Million Claims reserves were maintained 
at BDT 1,885.51 Million, ensuring strong provisioning 
discipline. During the year, claims paid exceeded BDT 
780 Million, with a claims settlement ratio of 17%, 
reaffirming our commitment to timely protection of 
policyholders.
Return on Equity (ROE) stood at 10% and Return on 
Assets (ROA) at 5%, reflecting steady performance 
despite capital market volatility and pricing pressures. 
Our customer retention rate remained above 70%, that 
indicates the sustainability of trust in our  brand.
These outcomes are a direct reflection of the 
dedication, adaptability, and professionalism of our 
employees. Their commitment to service excellence 
and ethical conduct remains the foundation of our 
continued progress.
Deepening Customer Focus and Expanding 
Access
Customer trust remains our most valuable asset. In 
2025, we strengthened our efforts to close Bangladesh’s 
insurance protection gap by expanding inclusive and 
accessible insurance solutions.
We enhanced microinsurance offerings, broadened 
SME-focused products, and scaled women-centric 
solutions such as Nibedita. Following the expansion 
of bancassurance partnerships, insurance accessibility 
increased significantly through collaboration with 
leading banks. These initiatives reflect our mission to 
democratize insurance and extend financial protection 
to underserved communities.
Governance, Compliance and Regulatory 
Alignment
The regulatory landscape continues to evolve, with 
stronger compliance expectations and governance 
standards. We remain fully aligned with directives of 
the Insurance Development and Regulatory Authority 
(IDRA), embedding transparency, accountability, and 
ethical practice into every operational layer.
Our governance framework integrates Environmental, 
Social, and Governance (ESG) considerations into 
underwriting, investment, and strategic planning. 
Enhanced compliance monitoring, internal audit 
reinforcement, and structured risk reporting have 
strengthened stakeholder confidence and reinforced 
our leadership position.
Advancing Digital Integration
Digital transformation accelerated meaningfully in 2025. 
We deployed a comprehensive CRM system enabling 
360-degree customer insights and predictive analytics. 
Our unified omnichannel platform streamlined 
engagement across mobile applications, web portals, 
and service centers, improving responsiveness and 
personalization.
AI-supported underwriting and claims analytics 
enhanced pricing accuracy and fraud detection 
capabilities. End-to-end digital policy issuance in 
key retail segments reduced turnaround time and 
improved customer convenience. More than half 
of customer interactions now occur through digital 
channels, reflecting a clear shift toward technology-
enabled service delivery.
Sustainability and Responsible Growth
Sustainability remains integral to our operating 
philosophy.
Environmental Commitment:
Digitalization initiatives reduced paper usage and 
operational emissions. We expanded climate-focused 
insurance products, including agricultural and weather-
index solutions, supporting resilience in vulnerable 
sectors.
Social Impact:
Our microinsurance and agricultural coverage 
programs continue to protect over 1.4 million farmers. 
Women-centric products and SME solutions empower 
entrepreneurs and strengthen financial inclusion 
nationwide.
Governance Excellence:
Strengthened anti-corruption frameworks, compliance 
systems, and risk oversight mechanisms ensure 
regulatory alignment and investor confidence.
Our sustainability initiatives continue to align business 
growth with long-term societal value creation.

2.6 BEHIND THE LEADERSHIP:  
STORIES OF OUR MANAGEMENT TEAM
Nasiruddin Ahmad Choudhury
Founding Managing Director
With more than half a century of experience, Mr. 
Nasiruddin Ahmad Choudhury is a pioneer of 
Bangladesh’s insurance industry and a widely respected 
business veteran.
He completed his Bachelor’s degree from Ananda 
Mohon College, Mymensingh, and earned a Master’s 
degree in Islamic History from the University of Dhaka. 
In September 1958, he joined the Pakistan Insurance 
Corporation in Karachi. He later received professional 
training in London and Germany, including specialized 
training at Munich Reinsurance Company. During 
his tenure at the Pakistan Insurance Corporation, he 
held several senior positions until the Liberation of 
Bangladesh.
In 1972, driven by a strong sense of patriotism and 
nation-building, Mr. Choudhury undertook the 
challenging responsibility of rebuilding the reinsurance 
department of Sadharan Bima Corporation as 
General Manager. After successfully achieving this 
objective, he left the organization in 1983 to pursue his 
entrepreneurial vision.
He also served as Insurance Adviser to Bangladesh 
Biman and Bangladesh Shipping Corporation for 
over 15 years. In 1985, following the opening of the 
insurance sector to private enterprises, Mr. Choudhury 
co-founded Green Delta Insurance PLC with a group 
of close associates, serving as its sponsor, Founder 
Managing Director, and CEO.
Throughout his illustrious career, Mr. Choudhury 
has received numerous national and international 
recognitions for his exceptional contributions to the 
insurance industry in Bangladesh and globally. In 2007, 
the U.S.-based International Who’s Who Historical 
Society recognized him as a Fellow. He has held 
several prestigious leadership roles, including Director 
of FBCCI, President of the Insurance Association of 
Bangladesh, Executive Member of the Metropolitan 
Chamber of Commerce and Industry, President of 
the Bangladesh-German Chamber of Commerce 
and Industry, and Chairman of Delta Brac Housing 
Finance Corporation. He also served as Chairman and 
Managing Director of NASCOM Private Limited.
Among his many accolades, he was honored by 
the Government of Bangladesh as a distinguished 
insurance personality for his outstanding contribution 
to the development of the insurance sector. His 
international awards include the International Quality 
Crown Award (Diamond Category) in London (2009), 
DHL–The Daily Star Lifetime Achievement Award 
(2009), Mother Teresa International Award (2019), and 
the International Star Award for Leadership in Quality 
in Paris. In 2014, he received the Lifetime Achievement 
Award at the 18th Asia Insurance Industry Awards. 
In 2020, Birla Institute of Management Technology 
(BIMTECH) conferred upon him another Lifetime 
Achievement Award for his outstanding contribution 
to Bangladesh’s insurance industry.
Mr. Choudhury has traveled extensively and maintains 
close professional associations with insurance 
experts across Germany, the UK, France, Japan, and 
Malaysia. Under his visionary mentorship, Green Delta 
Insurance has remained Bangladesh’s largest and 
most pioneering non-life insurer, introducing several 
industry-first innovations. These include Nibedita, an 
insurance product exclusively for women, weather 
index-based agriculture insurance, livestock insurance, 
and the establishment of a state-of-the-art insurance 
institute. Today, Green Delta Insurance continues 
to champion insurance inclusion with the mission of 
providing “Insurance for Everyone.”

Farzanah Chowdhury, a distinguished Chartered Insurer, 
leads Green Delta Insurance PLC, Bangladesh’s largest 
non-life insurance company. The company manages 
assets worth BDT 3 trillion (USD 33.3 billion) and serves 
over 1.2 million clients annually.
Under her leadership, Green Delta Insurance has 
maintained an “AAA” credit rating for 12 consecutive 
years, achieved Superbrand recognition since 2020, and 
received government commendation for exceptional 
claim settlement performance in 2022 and 2023. As the 
first female Managing Director and CEO in Bangladesh’s 
insurance sector, she is committed to creating value for 
both business and society through transparency, ethical 
governance, and inclusive growth.
Before assuming her current role, Ms. Chowdhury pioneered 
SME Banking at BRAC Bank Limited as Head of SME 
Banking, where she led innovative initiatives to expand 
financial services to marginalized communities. In 2016, 
she was recognized by the UN Global Compact as a Local 
SDG Pioneer for Women’s Economic Security for her work 
on Nibedita, a comprehensive insurance program designed 
for women. She also introduced micro-insurance services for 
rural populations, garment workers, and migrant workers.
Green Delta Insurance became the country’s first non-
life insurer to introduce digital insurance in 2018. In 
2020, it launched the sector’s first mobile app, followed 
by Bangladesh’s first full digital insurance ecosystem 
in 2023. Under her visionary leadership, the company 
has supported several government initiatives, including 
the Shasthya Suroksha Karmasuchi (SSK) project, which 
provides health insurance to low-income populations, 
benefiting over 200,000 households and more than 7 
million people living below the poverty line.
Green Delta Insurance has since evolved into a leading 
financial conglomerate, offering investment banking, 
brokerage, and wealth management services through 
subsidiaries such as Green Delta Capital Limited and 
Green Delta Securities Limited. GD Asset delivers 
healthcare services and global emergency medical 
evacuation support. The recent acquisition of Sun Life 
Insurance has further strengthened Green Delta’s position 
as a comprehensive financial solutions provider.
Ms. Chowdhury has received international recognition 
from the Chartered Insurance Institute (CII), UK, as a CII 
Goodwill Ambassador in Bangladesh. She also holds the 
Senior Associate designation from the Australian and 
New Zealand Institute of Insurance and Finance (ANZIIF). 
Selected through a competitive global process by the U.S. 
State Department, she participated in the International 
Women Leaders Mentoring Partnership Program in the 
United States and was mentored by ING Financial Services.
Her numerous accolades include Best CEO of the Year – 
Insurance at the South Asian Business Excellence Awards, Best 
CEO Award in the non-life insurance category, and Woman 
Leader of the Year at the 23rd Asia Insurance Industry Awards, 
making her the first Bangladeshi woman to receive this honor. 
She was also awarded the prestigious Public Trust Award by 
CII UK for Building Public Trust in Insurance – International.
Ms. Chowdhury holds key leadership roles across several 
organizations, including Advisory Board Member of the 
World Economic Forum’s New Champion Community, Private 
Sector Member of the Bangladesh Government Body of PKSF 
(2024–2025), and Global Chair of the Healthcare and Wellness 
Wing at G100. She serves as an Independent Director on the 
boards of DESCO, Bata Bangladesh, and Linde Bangladesh, 
and is a member of the Industry Advisory Board of North 
South University’s School of Business & Economics. She is also 
an Advisor and Mentor at the Australian Bangladesh Women 
Leadership Incorporated (ABWLI).
Through her continued leadership and advocacy, Ms. 
Chowdhury is transforming Bangladesh’s insurance 
landscape, advancing the mission of “Insurance for 
Everyone” to promote empowerment, inclusion, and 
sustainable development.

Mr. A.K.M. Iftekhar Ahmad has had a lifelong career

in 1971, the insurance Industry was nationalized and

Assistant Manager in 1973.

claims and branch and other departments till 1996 
when he voluntarily retired to join the private sector. 
In the private sector, he was the CEO of Eastern 
Insurance Co. Ltd. from 1998 to 2009 and CEO of 
Sonarbangla Insurance Co. Ltd. from 2010 to 2012. 
He retired from Sonarbangla on attaining the age of 
superannuation, i.e. 67 years. Thereafter, he joined 
Insurance Development and Regulatory Authority 
(IDRA) in July 2013 as a Senior Consultant and worked 
there till June 2016. He was also Member-Secretary 
of the Central Rating committee. During his tenure, 
Money Insurance Policy (MIP) was designed by the

piloted many new products for non-life insurance, such

Rating Committee and approved by IDRA.

of non-life insurance. He was also an elected member 
of the Executive Committee of Bangladesh Insurance

shaping the industry.

Entering 2025-marking 40 Years of Securing Tomorrows, 
Green Delta Insurance PLC reinforced its position 
as one of Bangladesh’s leading private-sector non-
life insurers. The Company delivered a resilient and 
disciplined performance across its divisions despite 
a dynamic socio-economic landscape, geopolitical 
uncertainty, regulatory evolution, and sector-specific 
challenges. Prudent underwriting, capital stewardship, 
and sustainable growth strategiesenable dsteady

Management Discussion and Analysis
In 2025, with four decades of Securing Tomorrows, 
Green Delta Insurance PLC navigated a challenging 
operating environment. Sustaining strong shareholder 
returns with a 27% cash dividend, Green Delta 
underscored prudent capital stewardship and 
commitment to long term value creation. Supported 
by robust governance and ESG integrated decision 
making, Green Delta strengthened risk management, 
advanced digital initiatives, and upheld high standards 
of transparency and accountability, as reflected in its 
SAFA Best Presented Annual Reports Gold Award 2025 
for excellence in financial reporting. This performance 
demonstrates the Company’s capacity to respond to 
evolving risks and opportunities, reinforce stakeholder 
confidence, and remain well positioned to protect 
present value and secure sustainable, inclusive growth 
for clients, shareholders, and society at large.

3.1.a.iv Industry Challenges
As Green Delta Insurance enters its 40th Year, the 
Company continues to operate within an insurance 
landscape shaped by structural and competitive 
challenges that require disciplined oversight and 
strategic response.
• Low Insurance Penetration and Awareness 
Risk
Insurance penetration in Bangladesh remains 
limited, constraining market depth and risk 
protection across large segments of the population. 
This presents a long-term industry challenge and a 
strategic opportunity. Green Delta addresses this 
through responsible insurance practices, targeted 
outreach, and simplified product offerings 
designed to broaden access while strengthening 
financial inclusion and societal resilience.
• Claims Credibility and Trust Deficit
Delayed or disputed claims settlement remains 
a systemic industry issue, with implications for 
consumer confidence and sector reputation. Green 
Delta mitigates this risk through governance-
led claims oversight, process automation, and 
transparent settlement practices, reinforcing trust 
as a core value proposition and a critical driver of 
long-term stakeholder confidence.
• Intensifying Competition and Pricing 
Pressure
Heightened competition and price-led market 
behaviour continue to exert pressure on 
underwriting margins. Rather than engaging in 
unsustainable price competition, Green Delta 
prioritises disciplined underwriting, value-added 
service differentiation, and risk-based pricing, 
supporting sustainable profitability, capital 
protection, and long-term value creation.
3.1.a.v. Risks & Opportunities 
Operating within a dynamic macroeconomic and industry 
landscape, Green Delta Insurance continuously evaluates 
emerging risks and growth opportunities through 
structured risk governance and strategic oversight, 
ensuring resilience and sustainable value creation.
Key Strategic Risks
• Macroeconomic Volatility
Inflationary pressures, exchange rate movements, 
and broader economic uncertainty may affect 
household and corporate purchasing power, 
influencing insurance demand and claims 
behaviour. The Company mitigates this risk through 
prudent underwriting, portfolio diversification, 
and capital discipline.
• Political and Regulatory Uncertainty
Evolving political dynamics and regulatory 
expectations may impact market sentiment and 
business continuity. Green Delta proactively 
engages with regulators and maintains robust

confidence.
Strategic Opportunities

market development.
• Digital Transformation and Innovation

Solutions

Changes to the financial statements are succinctly 
explained, complemented by a Management

Accounting Policies and Methods
In preparing its financial statements, Green Delta 
Insurance PLC applies accounting policies and 
estimates that are consistent, prudent, and fully aligned 
with applicable regulatory and financial reporting 
frameworks. These policies reflect the Company’s 
commitment to transparency, reliability, and sound 
financial governance.
• Revenue Recognition
Premium income is recognized in accordance with the 
accounting standards and guidelines prescribed by 
the Insurance Development and Regulatory Authority 
(IDRA) of Bangladesh, with appropriate provision 
made for unexpired risk to ensure accurate matching 
of income and risk exposure.
• Claims Reserves and Liabilities
Claims are recognized and provided for upon receipt of 
claim notifications. Adequate reserves are maintained 
to reflect the Company’s best estimate of outstanding 
liabilities, ensuring claims adequacy and balance sheet 
integrity.
• Investment Valuation
Investments, including fixed income securities and 
equities, are measured at fair value or amortized cost, as 
applicable, in line with relevant accounting standards. 
Valuation methodologies are consistently applied to 
reflect market conditions and risk characteristics.
• Reinsurance Accounting
Reinsurance arrangements are accounted for on 
a transparent basis, with premiums ceded and 
recoverable claims recognized accurately to reflect risk 
transfer and financial exposure.
• Asset Impairment
All assets, including investments, property, plant, 
and equipment, are subject to regular impairment 
assessments. Where indicators of impairment exist, 
recoverable amounts are determined using objective 
criteria and discounted cash flow analysis.
• Income Tax Accounting
Income tax is accounted for in compliance with the 
requirements of the National Board of Revenue (NBR) 
of Bangladesh, including the recognition of current and 
deferred tax assets and liabilities where applicable.
• Fair Value Measurement and Disclosure
The Company provides transparent disclosures on 
fair value measurement techniques, assumptions, and 
inputs used in valuing financial instruments and other 
relevant assets and liabilities.
• Regulatory Compliance
Green Delta Insurance maintains strict compliance with 
all regulatory requirements issued by IDRA, reinforcing 
strong governance, solvency discipline, and financial 
reporting integrity.
• Accounting Policy Changes and Estimates
Accounting policies and key estimates are reviewed on 
an ongoing basis to ensure they remain appropriate, 
robust, and aligned with International Financial 
Reporting Standards (IFRS) and evolving regulatory 
guidance. Any changes are implemented prudently 
to enhance the relevance, accuracy, and reliability of 
financial information, supporting informed stakeholder 
decision-making and long- term value creation.

As a responsible employer, Green Delta Insurance 
PLC (GDIPLC) remains committed to safeguarding 
employee welfare across all dimensions of employment. 
The company ensures equal opportunities for growth 
and development, fair and competitive compensation, 
strong health and safety standards, timely provident 
fund contributions, and employment terms that 
uphold fairness, transparency, and compliance with 
applicable regulations. Through these commitments, 
GDIPLC continues to foster a supportive and equitable

organizational sustainability.
Our employee orientation pin image: 
Compliance with labour laws to stop child 
labour contracts: 
GDIPLC maintains strict adherence to the labour laws 
of Bangladesh as part of its commitment to ethical 
and responsible business practices. The company fully 
complies with the provisions of the Bangladesh Labour 
Act, 2006, including the prohibition of child labour 
in any form of employment. By ensuring compliance 
with these legal requirements, GDIPLC reinforces its 
dedication to maintaining a workplace grounded in 
integrity, accountability, and social responsibility.
Employees participate in the company's 
community welfare programs, as do their family 
members:
Green Delta Insurance PLC continues to foster a 
culture of compassion and social responsibility by 
encouraging employees and their family members to 
actively participate in community welfare initiatives.
In 2025, employees once again demonstrated their 
commitment to society through meaningful volunteer 
engagement activities organized by the company.
During the summer season, employees participated 
in the distribution of drinking water across Dhaka city, 
supporting communities affected by extreme heat and 
ensuring access to a basic necessity.
During the winter season of 2025, Green Delta 
Insurance PLC organized a winter clothing distribution 
program to support underprivileged communities. 
Employees and their family members actively 
participated in distributing warm clothes, reinforcing 
the company’s commitment to humanitarian values 
and social responsibility.
These initiatives reflect our belief that corporate 
responsibility is best demonstrated through collective 
action and community engagement.
Commitment to labour laws concerning 
gratuities, provident funds, and WPPF: 
Green Delta Insurance PLC prioritizes the financial 
security and long-term well-being of its employees 
through structured benefit programs aligned with 
labour laws and organizational policies.
The company contributes 10% of employees’ basic 
salary each month to the provident fund. Employees 
who continue their service for more than five years 
after confirmation receive a doubled provident fund 
amount upon separation, recognizing their loyalty and 
contribution to the organization.
GDIPLC also provides gratuity benefits in accordance 
with company policy:
•	 Employees completing five or more years of 
service are entitled to one month’s last drawn 
basic salary for each completed year of service.
•	 Employees with ten or more years of service 
receive two months’ basic salary per year of 
service, subject to a maximum limit of 50 months’ 
basic salary.
The company is also progressing toward the 
implementation of a Workers Profit Participation 
Fund (WPPF). This initiative is intended to strengthen 
employee engagement by enabling employees to 
share in the organization’s success and reinforcing a 
participatory workplace culture.
Through these initiatives, GDIPLC continues to build a 
financially secure, motivated, and engaged workforce, 
supporting both employee well-being and long-term 
organizational growth.

Human Capital
Disclosure of general description of the policies and 
practices codified and adopted by the company 
with respect to Human Resource Development and 
Management relating to:
•	 Succession planning
Succession planning is an integral component of 
Green Delta Insurance PLC’s overall human resource 
planning process. To ensure leadership continuity and 
organizational sustainability, GDIPLC has adopted 
a structured and analytical approach to identifying, 
developing, and retaining capable and high-potential 
employees aligned with both current and future 
business objectives.
As part of the succession planning initiative launched 
in 2024, the company conducted a comprehensive job 
analysis covering approximately 40% of management-
level positions to identify critical functional areas 
and key roles within the organization. Based on this 
analysis, GDIPLC developed a competency framework 
outlining the knowledge, skills, and abilities required 
for these strategic roles.
Using the Nine Box Grid Model, the company identified 
high-potential employees and designed targeted 
development plans to support their continuous 
growth. The Learning and Development (L&D) Team 
is responsible for monitoring employee development 
progress and regularly updating the succession 
plan to ensure its effectiveness and alignment with 
organizational priorities.
Through this structured approach, GDIPLC continues 
to strengthen its leadership pipeline
and ensure long-term organizational resilience.
•	 Merit-Based Recruitment & Onboarding
Green Delta Insurance PLC (GDIPLC) follows a merit-
based recruitment and selection process designed to 
ensure that candidates are evaluated objectively and 
selected based on their qualifications, competencies, 
and suitability for the role. This approach enables the 
organization to attract and retain high-quality talent 
capable of contributing to long-term organizational 
success.
GDIPLC’s recruitment framework focuses on identifying 
the most suitable candidate through a structured 
and transparent evaluation process. Depending on 
the requirements of the position, candidates are 
assessed using multiple evaluation methods, including 
written examinations, interviews, presentations, 
and assessments of communication and language 
proficiency. These methods help ensure fairness, 
consistency, and alignment between candidate 
capabilities and job requirements.
The recruitment and selection process for regular 
employees typically follows a structured sequence 
of steps, ensuring efficiency, transparency, and 
compliance with organizational policies.

Annual Performance Appraisals System: 
At Green Delta Insurance PLC (GDIPLC), we 
implement the widely recognized Management by 
Objectives (MBO) framework to foster a structured and 
collaborative approach to performance evaluation. 
This framework facilitates the joint identification, 
planning, organization, and communication of key 
objectives between management and employees for 
the fiscal year.
Once objectives are defined, managers and 
employees participate in regular review sessions to 
monitor progress, evaluate goal feasibility, and ensure 
alignment with the organization’s strategic priorities. 
Goals are established and validated through the 
SMART KPI methodology, ensuring they are Specific, 
Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, and Time-bound.
Performance evaluations are conducted periodically, 
quarterly, semi-annually, or annually, based on 
the outcomes of the defined KPIs. Exceptional 
performance is recognized through promotions 
and salary adjustments, while employees requiring 
additional support receive targeted training and 
development programs to enhance their skills and 
overall performance.

thorough investigation, written communication 
of the outcome, and the opportunity to appeal 
decisions.
Our grievance policy is designed to guide 
employees in raising work-related concerns while 
assisting managers in addressing issues efficiently 
and impartially. This process ensures that all 
matters are handled with due diligence, fairness, 
and respect, promoting a positive, transparent, 
and accountable workplace culture.

4.5 MARKET MOVEMENTS: INSIGHTS FROM 
SHARE PRICE SENSITIVITY
Share Price sensitivity analysis with the Consequent Impact on the company’s earning 
The share price and market capitalization of Green Delta Insurance PLC during 2021–2025 demonstrate sensitivity 
to key earnings-related variables, including premium pricing, claims and operating costs, interest rate movements, 
and currency fluctuations. The peak share price in 2021 reflected strong underwriting performance and higher 
investment income amid favorable interest rates. The subsequent decline and stabilization during 2022–2023 
indicate margin pressure from increased claims costs and competitive premium pricing. In 2024, lower share prices 
corresponded with subdued investment returns and macroeconomic uncertainty. The modest recovery in 2025 
suggests improved earnings expectations supported by cost discipline, stabilized interest rates, and effective 
foreign currency risk management.

4.6 ENGAGING OUR STAKEHOLDERS: 
COMMUNICATION AND COLLABORATION
Green Delta Insurance PLC remains firmly committed to addressing the evolving needs of its stakeholders and to 
creating sustainable, long-term value for all those connected with the organization. Our value-generation strategy 
is anchored in the long-term welfare of policyholders, shareholders, employees, regulators, suppliers, communities, 
and society at large.
The Company’s approach to stakeholder value creation is outlined below:
•	 Ensuring a robust and stable treasury framework, while acting as responsible stewards of public funds and 
equipping customers with the knowledge required to make informed insurance decisions and achieve their 
financial objectives.
•	 Continuing awareness programmes to enhance insurance penetration and insurance-led protection, while 
ensuring that products remain affordable, accessible, and responsive to customer needs.
•	 Leveraging our scale and market presence to contribute to employment generation across the country.
•	 Embedding Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles across operations to deliver consistent 
and comprehensive socio-financial impact.
•	 Supporting disadvantaged and vulnerable communities through high-impact corporate citizenship initiatives.
•	 Contributing to national development through strict compliance with all statutory obligations, including timely 
payment of taxes.
•	 Supporting suppliers and small enterprises through fair and transparent procurement practices.
•	 Maintaining active participation in industry associations and trade bodies, contributing to the advancement 
of the insurance sector.

Publication of news in newspapers
In compliance with listing, financial reporting, and 
disclosure regulations, the Company publishes required 
information in multi-lingual national daily newspapers. 
This practice was duly followed throughout the year

Sharing information via quarterly reports
The Company maintains a structured reporting cycle 
by providing shareholders with quarterly, half-yearly, 
and annual reports, resulting in four comprehensive 
disclosures each year.
Policy on ensuring shareholder participation
Shareholders whose names appear in the Register of 
Members and/or Depository on the Record Date are 
entitled to attend the Annual General Meeting and 
receive dividends as approved.
In accordance with the Company’s Articles 
of Association, shareholders may appoint a 
proxy to attend and vote on their behalf. Duly 
completed and stamped proxy forms must 
be submitted at least 48 hours prior to the 
scheduled commencement of the meeting.  
 
Timeliness in Using Financial Statements and 
Holding AGM
• Timeliness of Financial Statements: 31st December 
of each calendar year.
• Timeliness of Holding AGM: Over the past decades, 
Green Delta Insurance PLC has been holding its 
AGM within 31st March, immediately after the 
completion of the financial year.
Plan for maximising attendance at the annual 
meeting of shareholders
Green Delta Insurance PLC publishes AGM notices 
in leading newspapers well in advance, providing 
shareholders with sufficient information to ensure 
effective participation. The AGM is held at a convenient 
time and accessible location.
The Annual Report and Notice of  AGM are 
disseminated in compliance with the Stock Exchanges 
Listing Regulations, 2015 and the Financial Reporting 
and Disclosure Act, 2018, allowing shareholders 
adequate time to review the materials, provide 
feedback, and participate meaningfully in discussions. 
This process also enables the Company to better 
understand material issues relevant to shareholders.
All shareholders are entitled to attend the Annual 
General Meeting, where they may interact directly with 
the Directors and share their views on the Company’s 
performance, future prospects, and other relevant 
matters. Shareholders are encouraged to attend in 
person or appoint proxies if unable to do so.
During the AGM, shareholders are given the 
opportunity to engage with Board members and offer 
suggestions. The chairman &  Chief Executive Officer 
and Managing Director responds to shareholder 
queries on behalf of the Board.
The method for distributing the schedule
In accordance with the Companies Act, 2020 (Second 
Amendment), hard copies of the Annual Report and 
AGM Notice are dispatched to shareholders on the 
Record Date at least 21 days prior to the AGM.
Notices of the AGM are also submitted to the 
Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission 
(BSEC), Dhaka Stock Exchange Limited (DSE), and 
Chittagong Stock Exchange Limited (CSE), and are 
published in both print and online media. Additionally, 
the AGM Notice is made available on the Company’s 
website to ensure broad accessibility.

4.7 OUR GUIDING PRINCIPLES: POLICIES AND 
PRACTICES THAT SHAPE US
At Green Delta Insurance PLC, a strong and well-defined framework of policies and practices forms the foundation 
of ethical conduct, sound governance, and operational excellence. These policies guide the Company’s day-to-day 
operations, ensure compliance with all applicable laws and regulatory requirements, promote a safe and inclusive 
workplace, and safeguard the values, culture, and integrity of the organization. Presented below are some of the key 
policies and practices adopted by the Company to ensure transparent, disciplined, and seamless business operations.
Whistle-blower
The whistle-blower policy is a vital element of 
Green Delta Insurance PLC’s corporate governance 
framework. It empowers employees at all levels to 
report unethical, unlawful, or improper conduct without 
fear of retaliation or victimization. The policy provides a 
secure and confidential channel for reporting concerns 
related to fraud, corruption, or other misconduct. By 
encouraging openness, accountability, and ethical 
behavior, the whistle-blower mechanism helps preserve 
the Company’s integrity, credibility, and reputation.
Sexual harassment
In line with the laws of Bangladesh and applicable 
international best practices, Green Delta Insurance PLC 
maintains a strict zero-tolerance policy against sexual 
harassment in the workplace. The policy clearly defines 
prohibited behavior, establishes formal procedures for 
lodging complaints, and ensures timely investigation and 
appropriate resolution. Support mechanisms are available 
for affected individuals, and disciplinary measures are 
enforced against offenders, fostering a safe, respectful, 
and dignified work environment for all employees.
Gender diversity
Green Delta Insurance PLC recognizes gender diversity 
as a key driver of innovation, performance, and 
sustainable growth. The Company has implemented 
policies and practices to promote gender equality 
and inclusion across recruitment, career development, 
and leadership opportunities. These initiatives aim to 
eliminate bias and ensure fair representation in decision-
making processes. By nurturing a diverse and inclusive 
workforce, the Company strengthens its organizational 
culture and better reflects the society it serves.
Insider trading
To safeguard market integrity and protect stakeholder 
interests, Green Delta Insurance PLC has established robust 
insider trading policies. These policies prohibit employees, 
directors, and other insiders from trading in securities based 
on material, non-public, or price-sensitive information 
relating to the Company or its stakeholders. Clear reporting 
obligations and trading restrictions are outlined to ensure 
full compliance with regulatory requirements and to 
maintain investor confidence in the Company.
Code of conduct
The Company’s Code of Conduct sets out the ethical 
standards and behavioral expectations applicable 
to all employees, executives, and directors of Green 
Delta Insurance PLC. It emphasizes principles such as 
honesty, integrity, professionalism, accountability, and 
respect for diversity. The Code also provides guidance 
on managing conflicts of interest, acceptance of gifts, 
and compliance with applicable laws and regulations. 
By embedding ethical values into everyday decision-
making, the Code of Conduct reinforces stakeholder 
trust and enhances the Company’s corporate 
reputation.
Code of conduct
The Company’s Code of Conduct sets out the ethical 
standards and behavioral expectations applicable 
to all employees, executives, and directors of Green 
Delta Insurance PLC. It emphasizes principles such as 
honesty, integrity, professionalism, accountability, and 
respect for diversity. The Code also provides guidance 
on managing conflicts of interest, acceptance of gifts, 
and compliance with applicable laws and regulations. 
By embedding ethical values into everyday decision-
making, the Code of Conduct reinforces stakeholder 
trust and enhances the Company’s corporate 
reputation.
Data protection and privacy
Given the sensitive nature of policyholder and 
stakeholder information handled by the Company, 
data protection and privacy remain a critical priority for 
Green Delta Insurance PLC. The data protection and 
privacy policies govern the collection, use, storage, 
and disclosure of personal and confidential information 
in accordance with prevailing laws and industry best 
practices. These policies establish robust safeguards 
against unauthorized access, data breaches, and 
misuse, thereby protecting customer information, 
maintaining trust, and ensuring regulatory compliance.
Through this comprehensive framework of policies and 
practices, Green Delta Insurance PLC upholds the highest 
standards of corporate governance, ethics, integrity, 
and compliance. From whistle-blower protection and 
workplace safety to diversity, data privacy, and ethical 
business conduct, these guiding principles reflect the 
Company’s unwavering commitment to transparency, 
accountability, and responsible insurance practices, 
reinforcing its position as a trusted and responsible 
corporate citizen in Bangladesh.

4.10 INVESTOR-FRIENDLY INSIGHTS: 
SIMPLIFYING KEY INFORMATION
To support clear understanding and informed decision-making, Green Delta Insurance PLC (GDIPLC) presents key 
financial and operational indicators in a simplified and investor-friendly format. These highlights offer a concise 
snapshot of the Company’s performance, profitability, and shareholder value creation.
Net Profit Margin
Net profit margin reflects the Company’s ability to convert revenue into profit after 
covering all operating and non-operating expenses. For investors, this ratio is 
a key indicator of operational efficiency and pricing discipline. Higher and stable 
margins generally translate into stronger shareholder returns. GDIPLC continuously 
monitors profitability across products and compares performance against industry 
benchmarks to ensure sustainable growth and value creation.
Dividend
Dividend payments represent a tangible return to shareholders and reflect the 
Company’s confidence in its financial strength and future prospects. GDIPLC has 
maintained a consistent dividend-paying track record, balancing shareholder 
expectations with capital adequacy and growth requirements. The Board and 
management remain committed to rewarding shareholder trust while ensuring long-
term financial resilience.
Return on Equity
Return on Equity (ROE) measures GDIPLC’s effectiveness in generating profits from 
shareholders’ investments. It highlights how efficiently equity capital is deployed 
to support business operations and expansion. A strong ROE reflects prudent 
management, disciplined capital allocation, and effective underwriting and 
investment strategies. During the year, GDIPLC achieved an ROE of 10%.
Debt to Equity
The debt-to-equity ratio indicates the proportion of financing sourced from 
creditors relative to shareholders’ equity. This metric helps investors assess the 
Company’s financial leverage and risk profile. A higher ratio suggests greater 
reliance on borrowed funds, while a lower ratio reflects a more equity-driven capital 
structure. GDIPLC maintains a balanced approach to leverage in line with regulatory 
requirements and prudent risk management practices.

Net Claims
Net claims represent the total benefits paid or payable to policyholders or 
beneficiaries under insurance contracts, net of reinsurance recoveries. During the 
year, net claims amounted to BDT 394 million, reflecting GDIPLC’s commitment to 
honoring claims promptly and supporting policyholders when it matters most.
Gross Premium
Gross premium represents the total premium income generated from insurance 
policies issued during the accounting period. It reflects the scale of GDIPLC’s 
underwriting activities and market reach. Gross general insurance premium for 
the year amounted to BDT 5,400 million, demonstrating the Company’s continued 
presence and competitiveness in the insurance market.

4.22 REWARDING SHAREHOLDERS:  
OUR DIVIDEND DISTRIBUTION POLICY
This policy will be applicable to Green Delta Insurance 
PLC (“The Company”). This policy is for declaration 
and payment of dividend to shareholders of the 
company. Further, Dividend Policies of the subsidiaries, 
wherever applicable, will be in line of the company’s 
Dividend policy and confirmed by the respective Board 
of Directors.
Declaration
Dividend shall be declared or paid out of
i. Current Year’s profit
a. After providing for depreciation and Tax in 
accordance with law.
b. After transferring to the reserves such amount 
of Profit as may be prescribed, or
ii. The Profits for any previous financial year(s)
a. After providing for depreciation in accordance 
with law, and
b. Remaining undistributed.
c. If the current year’s profit is not adequate, 
then the company may declare dividend out 
of accumulated distributable from previous 
year or
iii. Out of i) & ii) both
Board should avoid the practice of payment of dividend 
from borrowings except for meeting timing difference 
between payments of dividend and generating positive 
cash flows provided there is sufficient profit generated. 
Wide variation in rate of dividend should be avoided.
Dividend Equalization Reserve 
A dividend equalization reserve may be created by 
appropriating a portion of the distributable profit 
from time to time to enable the company to maintain 
consistency in distribution of dividend from year to 
year. In cases where there is inadequacy for current 
profit for payment of desired dividend amount then it 
may be transferred from this account to distributable 
profit to maintain consistency in dividend distribution.
Factors to be considered before declaration of 
Dividend 
The Company strive to distribute the best possible 
consolidated Profit After Tax (PAT) as dividend. 
However, since the company is in the initial stage of 
growth trajectory substantial Capital including internal 
accruals is required to be reinvested. Therefore, Board 
for next 3 years would exercise discretion in declaring 
the dividend based upon the requirement of capital for 
its portfolio business. The amounts paid as dividends 
in the past will not be necessarily indicative of the 
dividend amounts, if any that may be payable in future. 
The form, frequency and amount of future dividends 
shall be at the discretion of our Board and subject to 
the approval of our shareholders and will depend on 
various factors including but not limited to:
1. Revenues;
2. Cash Flows;
3. Financial Condition (including capital position);
4. Capital requirements;
5. Profit earned during the financial year;
6. Liquidity;
7. Future expansion plans;
8. Applicable taxes on dividend in hands of recipients 
including dividend distribution tax, where applicable;
9. Retained earnings vs. expected return from the 
business;
10. Adequate cash utilization opportunities
Timing of Dividend
1) Interim dividends as and when decided by 
Board will be declared after considering 
the interim P&L Account and Balance Sheet 
statement for the period for which interim 
dividends are declared. Interim P&L Account 
and Balance Sheet Statement will be prepared 
considering the profit, depreciation for the 
full year, taxation including the differed tax 
and any anticipated losses for the year. 
2) Final dividends as and when declared at the 
AGM of the shareholders will be based on the 
recommendations by Board based on review 
of audited financial statements of the year.

4.23 TRACKING UNCLAIMED DIVIDENDS: 
SUMMARY AND UPDATES
Green Delta Insurance PLC (GDIPLC) follows a structured and transparent framework for managing unpaid and 
unclaimed dividends in full compliance with the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC) Directive 
on “Dividend Distribution and Management of Unpaid and Unclaimed Dividends” (Notification No. BSEC/
CMMRRCD/2021-386/03 dated January 14, 2021).
In accordance with the directive, all unclaimed cash dividends are maintained in a separate designated bank 
account for a period of three (3) years from the date of approval at the Annual General Meeting (AGM). During this 
period, dividends are paid to shareholders upon successful verification of claims. Upon expiry of the prescribed 
timeline, any unclaimed dividends are transferred to the Capital Market Stabilization Fund (CMSF) established 
by the BSEC. In the event of a valid claim after such transfer, GDIPLC facilitates recovery from CMSF and ensures 
payment to the rightful shareholder.

Transparency and accountability are central to the 
governance philosophy of Green Delta Insurance PLC. 
The Annual General Meeting (AGM) serves as a key

and responsible stewardship to shareholders and 
stakeholders.

transparent disclosure of its corporate governance 
framework, risk management practices, and compliance 
policies. The Company clearly articulates its dedication 
to regulatory adherence, ethical standards, and 
the protection of shareholder interests, reinforcing 
confidence in its governance processes.

reporting, operational oversight, and strategic 
decision-making. Robust mechanisms are maintained 
to prevent conflicts of interest, promote fairness, and 
uphold the integrity of the organization. Through these 
measures, Green Delta continues to strengthen trust 
and accountability across all levels of the Company.
Equally important is the Company’s proactive approach 
to shareholder engagement. Green Delta encourages 
constructive dialogue, actively considers shareholder

responsiveness, fostering a culture of openness and 
mutual respect.
By clearly disclosing these policies and practices 
at the AGM, Green Delta reaffirms its unwavering
