RE INSURANCE ARRANGEMENT WITH 
LOCAL AND REPUTED FOREIGN COMPANY’S 
TREATY LIMIT
Reinsurance forms a fundamental pillar of the risk 
management architecture of Green Delta Insurance 
PLC. Through prudent and well-structured reinsurance 
arrangements, the Company mitigates concentration 
risk, enhances underwriting capacity, and safeguards 
its solvency position.
Reinsurance enables the transfer of a defined portion 
of the risks assumed by the Company (the ceding 
insurer) to other insurance or reinsurance entities. 
These arrangements are structured in alignment with 
the Company’s risk appetite, capital management 
objectives, and regulatory requirements, while ensuring 
diversification across both domestic and internationally 
reputed reinsurance partners.
Strategic Objectives of Reinsurance
•	 Capital Protection: Limiting net exposure to 
catastrophic or large individual losses.
•	 Earnings Stability: Reducing volatility in claims 
experience across financial periods.
•	 Capacity Enhancement: Enabling the underwriting 
of large or complex risks beyond the Company’s 
standalone retention capacity.
•	 Regulatory Compliance: Supporting solvency and 
capital adequacy requirements.
The Company’s reinsurance program is reviewed 
annually to ensure optimal retention levels, cost 
efficiency, and alignment with evolving market 
conditions.
Types of Reinsurance Arrangements
1. Facultative Reinsurance
Facultative reinsurance is arranged on an individual 
risk or policy basis. Under this structure, the Company 
selectively cedes specific risks, typically those that 
are high-value, specialized, or outside standard 
underwriting parameters.
Each facultative placement is separately negotiated 
and underwritten by the reinsurer, allowing flexibility 
in structuring coverage for unique or large-scale 
exposures.
2. Treaty Reinsurance
Treaty reinsurance involves a pre-agreed arrangement 
under which the reinsurer automatically accepts 
a defined category of risks under specified terms 
and conditions. This structure provides efficiency, 
predictability, and systematic risk transfer. Treaty 
arrangements are generally classified into the following 
categories:
I. Proportional Treaty Reinsurance
Under proportional treaties, the reinsurer shares 
premiums and claims in an agreed proportion. 
Common forms include:
•	 Quota Share: A fixed percentage of every 
policy within the treaty is ceded to the 
reinsurer.
•	 Surplus Share: The reinsurer accepts risk 
amounts exceeding the Company’s retention 
up to a defined limit.
This structure ensures balanced risk distribution 
while providing consistent underwriting support.
II. Non-Proportional Treaty Reinsurance
Under non-proportional arrangements, the 
reinsurer’s liability arises only when claims exceed 
a specified retention threshold. Premium sharing 
is not directly proportional to the risk ceded. 
REINSURANCE
ANNUAL REPORT 2025
GREEN DELTA INSURANCE PLC
216
Common forms include:
•	 Excess of Loss (XoL): The reinsurer indemnifies 
losses exceeding a predetermined retention 
up to a contractual limit.
•	 Stop Loss: Protection is triggered when 
aggregate claims exceed a defined loss ratio 
or monetary threshold within a specified 
period.
Non-proportional treaties are particularly effective in 
protecting against catastrophic losses and abnormal 
claims volatility.
Commitment to Prudent Risk Transfer
The Company maintains a diversified panel of financially 
sound reinsurers with strong credit ratings and proven 
claims-paying ability. Reinsurance placements are 
structured to optimize capital efficiency while ensuring 
timely recovery of claims.
Through disciplined reinsurance management, Green 
Delta Insurance PLC enhances its financial resilience, 
supports sustainable underwriting growth, and 
reinforces its commitment to policyholder protection 
and long-term stability.
Treaty Limits 
Treaty limits represent a critical component of the 
Company’s reinsurance framework, defining the 
maximum liability assumed by reinsurers under 
specific treaty arrangements. These limits are carefully 
structured to align with the Company’s retention 
capacity, capital strength, and overall risk appetite.
At Green Delta Insurance PLC, treaty limits are 
determined through rigorous portfolio analysis, 
catastrophe modeling, and stress testing to ensure 
optimal risk transfer while maintaining capital efficiency.
Proportional Treaty Limits
Under proportional treaty arrangements, the reinsurer’s 
participation is defined by an agreed percentage share 
of premiums and corresponding claims. The treaty limit 
may be expressed in terms of:
• A fixed percentage of each risk ceded (e.g., Quota 
Share arrangements), or
• A surplus capacity above the Company’s net 
retention up to a specified monetary ceiling (e.g., 
Surplus Share arrangements).
This structure ensures balanced risk-sharing and 
predictable cost allocation between the Company and 
its reinsurance partners.
Non-Proportional Treaty Limits
In non-proportional arrangements, such as Excess of 
Loss treaties, the treaty limit is typically defined as a 
monetary threshold. The reinsurer becomes liable only 
when losses exceed the Company’s pre-determined 
retention, up to the contractual limit specified in the 
treaty.
This framework provides effective protection against 
large individual losses and catastrophic events, thereby 
stabilizing earnings and safeguarding solvency.
Through prudent determination of treaty limits and 
periodic review of retention levels, the Company 
maintains a disciplined and resilient reinsurance 
structure that supports sustainable underwriting 
growth and long-term financial stability.
Disclosure of Extent of Risk Retained and 
Reinsured
Effective risk allocation between retained and 
reinsured portions is fundamental to the financial 
strength and underwriting discipline of Green Delta 
Insurance PLC. The Company adopts a structured 
risk retention strategy that balances profitability with 
capital protection, ensuring sustainable growth and 
resilience against adverse events.
Retained Risk
Retained risk represents the portion of exposure that 
the Company elects to keep on its own account, 
without transferring it to reinsurers. The level of 
retention is determined based on:
• Capital adequacy and solvency position
• Portfolio diversification and loss experience
• Nature and volatility of the underlying risk
• Regulatory requirements and internal risk appetite
Retention levels are periodically reviewed to ensure 
alignment with the Company’s financial capacity and 
strategic objectives. While retained risk offers the 
opportunity to enhance underwriting margins and 
profitability, it also requires prudent monitoring to 
safeguard against excessive exposure.
Reinsured Risk
Reinsured risk refers to the portion of exposure transferred 
to reinsurers under structured reinsurance arrangements. 
In exchange for a share of the premium, reinsurers assume 
liability for losses exceeding the Company’s retention, 
subject to agreed treaty terms and limits.
• This strategic transfer of risk serves multiple 
objectives:

Ceded Premiums
Ceded premiums represent the portion of gross 
written premiums transferred to reinsurers in exchange 
for reinsurance protection. These premiums constitute 
a direct cost of risk transfer and are recognized as an 
expense in the determination of net premium revenue.
The level of ceded premiums reflects:
• The Company’s retention strategy and capital 
management approach
• The structure and scope of treaty and facultative 
arrangements
• The scale and volatility of underlying risk exposures
Transparent disclosure of ceded premiums enables 
stakeholders to assess the balance between retained 
and transferred risk, as well as the efficiency of 
capital utilization. A well-structured reinsurance 
program ensures that the cost of reinsurance remains 
proportionate to the level of risk mitigation achieved.

Operations & Claims Management Practices: /
(Preface)
Insurance operates through a structured contractual 
relationship under which the insurer undertakes the 
responsibility of compensating the policyholder (the 
insured) for losses covered under the terms of the 
policy. This framework is built on the principle of 
risk sharing, whereby financial losses are collectively 
managed through pooled resources contributed 
by policyholders. The effectiveness and efficiency 
of claims handling play a decisive role in shaping 
an insurer’s credibility and public perception, as 
weaknesses in this area can erode confidence and 
adversely affect reputation. Consequently, the claims 
function represents a critical point of interaction where 
policyholders directly experience the practical value 
and reliability of insurance protection.
The insurance policy serves as formal and legal 
documentation of the contractual obligations between 
the insurer and the insured, ensuring transparency, 
clarity, and certainty for both parties. It clearly defines the 
applicable terms, conditions, exclusions, exceptions, and 
warranties associated with the relevant class of insurance. 
Precise, accurate, and unambiguous policy wording is 
essential to minimize disputes, avoid misinterpretation, 
and ensure consistency during claim assessment, 
including the determination of the proximate cause of 
loss. In this regard, the policy schedule holds particular 
importance, as it must clearly and comprehensively 
present all material information in a complete, accurate, 
and self-explanatory manner to prevent misunderstanding 
and facilitate efficient claims processing.
Claims management remains one of the most critical 
operational functions of an insurance company and 
serves as a key indicator of overall service quality, 
operational discipline, and efficiency. In the non-life 
insurance segment, where a wide range of traditional 
as well as specialized insurance products are offered, 
claims handling procedures vary significantly 
depending on the nature, cause, complexity, and 
severity of each loss. As a result, strong and consistent 
claims management capabilities provide a meaningful 
competitive advantage and are highly valued by 
policyholders. The fair, transparent, and timely 
settlement of valid claims continues to be the primary 
reason customers place their trust and confidence in 
insurance solutions.
Green Delta Insurance follows a structured and well-
defined approach to claims management, guided by 
a corporate philosophy that emphasizes efficiency, 
transparency, fairness, and customer service excellence. 
This framework establishes clear service standards and 
integrates IT -enabled systems to facilitate effective 
monitoring, tracking, and control of claims throughout 
the entire settlement lifecycle, from notification to final 
resolution.
Overall, claims management encompasses both 
operational services and advisory support related 
to compensation, restitution, repayment, or other 
remedies arising from insured losses. It also plays an 
important role in supporting policyholders during 
loss events by ensuring clarity, guidance, and timely 
communication. Alongside underwriting, claims 
settlement constitutes one of the two fundamental 
pillars underpinning the Company’s insurance 
operations and long-term sustainability

The Claims Process
Insurance claims, whether simple or complex, pass 
through several procedural stages. As each claim 
differs in nature, no single method applies to all cases. 
Every claim must therefore be assessed individually, 
based on its specific facts and circumstances, using 
careful and prudent judgment. 
An insurer occupies a position of trust, as it manages 
funds collected from policyholders through premiums. 
This requires the insurer to act fairly and responsibly, 
ensuring that the insured or claimant receives 
accurate indemnity, neither more nor less than what is 
contractually due.
A policyholder pays a premium with the expectation 
that financial losses arising from insured risks will be 
compensated according to the policy terms.
The claims process starts when a loss is reported to 
Green Delta Insurance. The company promptly appoints 
a licensed loss adjuster and accepts claim notifications 
24/7 through multiple channels. A preliminary survey 
is conducted to assess potential liability, and insured 
parties are requested to submit all required documents 
without delay. Standard documentation requirements 
are maintained at the Head Office for each class of 
insurance.
Green Delta Insurance follows a structured claims 
management process, including communication with 
the insured, loss inspection, assessment of damage, 
and determination of liability. Clients are also advised 
on loss prevention and salvage protection.
Once all necessary documents and the final survey 
report are received, the claim is reviewed and settled 
promptly if found in order. Provisions are maintained 
for any claims outstanding at the end of the accounting 
period.
Due to its effective claims settlement performance, 
Green Delta Insurance has been awarded a AAA rating 
for claims payability by the Credit Rating Agency of 
Bangladesh Limited (CRAB).

Claims Management and Claims Handling
Claims management refers to the complete administration 
of the claims process, from initial notification through to 
performance evaluation. This includes monitoring claim-
related expenses, legal costs, and settlement outcomes. 
In the case of self-insurers, claims management also 
involves implementing measures to reduce future losses 
and overall claims costs.
Claims handling, on the other hand, is a traditional term 
that focuses primarily on claim review, investigation, 
and negotiation. It does not extend to broader risk 
management considerations.
Policyholder Expectations
Under an insurance contract, a policyholder reasonably 
expects:
•	 Adequate insurance coverage at an 
appropriate premium
•	 Timely issuance of accurate policy documents 
with clear guidance
•	 Prompt and satisfactory settlement of claims 
when a loss occurs
Role of the Claims Department
The efficiency of claim settlement serves as a key 
indicator of an insurance company’s commitment to 
customer service. Claims must therefore be settled 
fairly, efficiently, and without unnecessary delay. Each 
insurer follows its own principles and procedures for 
claims administration, which may vary across different 
classes of insurance.
The claims department plays a central role in the 
insurer’s operations, with responsibilities including:
•	 Strategic role: Delivering high-quality service 
to gain competitive advantage or justify 
outsourcing when necessary
•	 Cost control: Ensuring claim payments remain 
within contractual limits
•	 Customer service: Meeting or exceeding 
customer expectations in terms of speed, 
professionalism, and cost efficiency
•	 Management role: Maintaining service 
standards while operating within budgetary 
limits
Reinsurance and Claims Handling
A key distinction exists between insurance and 
reinsurance claims handling. Reinsurance claims 
typically involve negotiations between insurance 
professionals, often within long-term business 
relationships. In contrast, insurance claims usually 
involve negotiation with members of the public, 
where future relationships may depend heavily on the 
outcome of the claim. For large or complex claims, 
specialists, lawyers, or consultants may represent one 
or both parties.
Outstanding Claims (IBNR and IBNER) and 
Their Ageing
In addition to claims settled within an accounting 
period, insurers may have outstanding claim liabilities. 
These liabilities arise from claims that have been 
incurred but not yet reported (IBNR) or reported but 
not yet fully settled or adequately reserved (IBNER).
Delays in claim settlement generally occur due to two 
main reasons:
(i) Reporting delay, which refers to the time gap 
between the occurrence of a loss and its reporting to 
the insurer; and
(ii) Settlement delay, as adequate assessment of the 
total claim amount requires time. Depending on the 
nature of the insurance, the period between loss 
occurrence and final settlement may range from a few 
days to several years, particularly in liability insurance.
To meet future claim obligations, insurers create 
provisions by setting aside a portion of the net 
premium. These provisions ensure the insurer’s ability 
to settle all valid claims arising from insured events. 
The provision for outstanding claims is commonly 
calculated using the following formula:

For sound accounting practice, reserves are maintained 
for outstanding claims for each financial year. In 
practice, the terms IBNR and IBNER are sometimes 
used interchangeably, and in certain markets, especially 
reinsurance, IBNR may include IBNER. Accordingly, 
the liability for outstanding claims presented in the 
balance sheet of a non-life insurance company includes 
provisions for both IBNR and IBNER.
IBNR represents an estimate of losses from insured 
events that have occurred before the accounting date 
but have not yet been reported. As the frequency and 
severity of such claims are unknown, IBNR is necessarily 
an estimate. The accuracy of this estimation is often 
regarded as an indicator of an insurer’s financial and 
actuarial strength.
IBNER refers to additional reserves required for claims 
that have already been reported but where the initially 
established reserves are insufficient. This typically 
applies to claims where the ultimate cost becomes 
clear only over time, such as long-term liability or 
workers’ compensation claims. Insurers regularly 
review and adjust these reserves as new information 
becomes available.
Green Delta Insurance maintains adequate provisions 
for all outstanding claims, including ageing analysis. 
In compliance with directives issued by the Insurance 
Development and Regulatory Authority (IDRA) of 
Bangladesh, the company submits quarterly reports on 
outstanding claims, their ageing, and the reasons for 
any settlement delays.
Although current insurance laws in Bangladesh do 
not mandate separate reserves for IBNR and IBNER, 
such provisions are expected to become compulsory 
under the solvency margin framework proposed in the 
Insurance Act 2010.
Solvency Margin Disclosure
The solvency margin represents the excess of an 
insurer’s assets over its liabilities and reflects the 
insurer’s capacity to meet claim obligations. Regulatory 
standards prescribe valuation methods and minimum 
solvency requirements to ensure financial stability. 
Maintaining adequate technical reserves and sufficient 
capital is essential to safeguarding solvency.
The solvency ratio, commonly calculated as Net Assets 
÷ Net Written Premium, measures the insurer’s ability 
to absorb risk. Although IDRA has not yet specified a 
mandatory solvency margin level, insurers are expected 
to maintain strong solvency positions to ensure long-
term financial soundness.

Disclosures pertaining to Solvency Margin
The solvency margin is a critical measure of financial 
resilience, representing the excess of an insurer’s 
admissible assets over its liabilities. It serves as a financial 
buffer, ensuring that the Company can meet policyholder 
obligations under both normal and adverse conditions.
In Bangladesh, the Insurance Development and Regulatory 
Authority (IDRA) mandates solvency margin requirements 
for all life and non-life insurers, promoting financial stability 
and safeguarding policyholder interests. For non-life 
insurers, this encompasses coverage for underwriting risk, 
investment risk, and potential catastrophic events such as 
natural disasters or large-scale claims.
Maintaining a robust solvency margin allows the 
Company to honor claims reliably, even during 
economic downturns, thereby reducing the risk of 
insolvency. Under IDRA’s risk-based capital framework, 
insurers are required to continuously assess their 
financial position and implement corrective actions if 
the solvency margin falls below regulatory thresholds.
By ensuring compliance with solvency requirements, 
Green Delta Insurance PLC reinforces policyholder 
confidence, strengthens its financial stability, and 
upholds its commitment to responsible and sustainable 
insurance practices.

6.2.7 INVESTMENT STRATEGY & ASSET 
MANAGEMENT: BUILDING SUSTAINABLE VALUE
Valuation and Impairment of Investments: Regulatory 
Compliance and Financial Prudence
At Green Delta Insurance PLC, rigorous valuation 
and impairment assessment of investments is central 
to financial stability, regulatory compliance, and 
policyholder protection. In line with the Insurance 
Act 2010 and directives issued by the Insurance 
Development and Regulatory Authority (IDRA), the 
Company regularly evaluates its investment portfolio 
to ensure accurate financial reporting and prudent risk 
management.
Investment Portfolio and Impairment 
Assessment
The Company’s investment portfolio comprises 
government securities, fixed deposits, equities, and 
real estate, all of which are subject to market, credit, 
and economic risks. Impairment arises when the 
recoverable amount of an investment falls below its 
carrying value due to these factors.
Upon identification of an impairment, the associated 
loss is recognized in the profit and loss account, and 
the carrying value of the asset is adjusted accordingly. 
This approach ensures transparency, prevents 
overstatement of financial strength, and protects 
policyholder interests.
Compliance with IFRS 9
Valuation and impairment testing are conducted in 
accordance with IFRS 9, enabling the Company to:
• Maintain a realistic assessment of asset values.
• Ensure solvency and adequate capital 
coverage.
• Comply with regulatory capital requirements 
and reporting standards.
Through disciplined investment management, timely 
impairment recognition, and adherence to regulatory 
frameworks, Green Delta Insurance PLC reinforces its 
commitment to financial prudence, transparency, and 
sustainable policyholder protection.
Disclosure of Encumbrances On Assets
At Green Delta Insurance PLC, transparency and financial 
integrity are paramount. Disclosure of encumbrances 
on assets is critical to provide stakeholders with a clear 
understanding of any legal, contractual, or regulatory 
restrictions that may affect the Company’s ability to 
utilize its assets for claim settlements, investments, or 
liquidity management. Given the non-life insurance 
context, where maintaining adequate reserves for 
policyholder obligations is essential, encumbrances 
directly influence financial stability and solvency.
Types of Encumbrances
•	 Mortgages and Liens: Real estate or fixed assets 
held by the Company may be subject to mortgages 
or liens, which can restrict the ability to liquidate 
these assets during periods of financial stress.
•	 Pledged Investments: Certain investment 
securities may be pledged as collateral for loans, 
reinsurance arrangements, or other financing 
agreements, limiting their availability for claim 
payouts.
•	 Legal and Regulatory Restrictions: Assets may be 
encumbered due to ongoing litigation, regulatory 
directives, or contractual obligations with 
reinsurers, impacting their immediate usability.
•	 Collateral for Reinsurance: Reinsurance 
agreements often require collateral deposits, 
which restrict direct access to these funds and 
affect liquidity management.
Impact on Financial Reporting and Solvency
Encumbrances influence asset liquidity, valuation, and 
overall risk exposure. Transparent disclosure ensures 
that policyholders, regulators, and stakeholders are 
fully informed of potential constraints on the Company’s 
resources. Proper reporting facilitates:
Accurate assessment of solvency and liquidity positions
Compliance with regulatory standards, including IFRS 
17 and local insurance legislation
Informed decision-making by management and 
stakeholders
By maintaining clear and detailed disclosure of asset 
encumbrances, Green Delta Insurance PLC reinforces 
its commitment to transparency, regulatory compliance, 
and the protection of policyholder interests.

6.3.1 Our Internal Control Structure: Ensuring Operational Excellence
Information of the Internal Control System
The Internal Control System of the organization is 
designed to enhance the reliability and integrity of 
financial and non-financial information and to ensure 
effective governance across all operations. The system 
provides reasonable assurance regarding compliance 
with approved policies, plans, procedures, applicable 
laws, and regulatory requirements.
In addition, the internal control framework safeguards 
the organization’s assets, promotes the economical 
and efficient use of resources, and supports the 
achievement of established operational objectives 
and strategic goals. Through clearly defined controls, 
accountability mechanisms, and continuous oversight, 
the system contributes to disciplined operations, 
risk mitigation, and sustainable organizational 
performance.
Strengthening Integrity Through Robust 
Internal Controls
At Green Delta Insurance PLC (GDIPLC), we are 
firmly committed to fostering a culture of integrity, 
accountability, and transparency through a strong and 
effective internal control system. This system forms the 
foundation of our operational framework, ensuring 
efficiency, transparency, and full compliance with 
applicable laws, regulations, and internal policies.
Through continuous monitoring of business processes 
and regular evaluation of control effectiveness, we seek 
to mitigate risks, safeguard the reliability of financial 
reporting, and ensure timely, accurate, and appropriate 
disclosure of information to all stakeholders.
Compliance as a Strategic Imperative
We recognize that compliance extends beyond 
regulatory obligation and represents a fundamental 
driver of long-term organizational success. In an 
increasingly regulated and closely scrutinized business 
environment, a strong commitment to ethical conduct 
and regulatory adherence is essential to maintaining 
stakeholder confidence and trust.
At GDIPLC, we pursue consistent and comprehensive 
compliance across all operations, recognizing its 
direct contribution to strengthening our social and 
relationship capital.
Investing in Compliance for Long-Term Value 
Creation
While the development and maintenance of a robust 
compliance framework require significant financial and 
infrastructural investment, we view such commitments 
as long-term value-enhancing initiatives. Proactive 
management of compliance risks strengthens our 
intellectual and human capital by promoting ethical 
behavior, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Although short-term impacts on financial and 
manufacturing capital may arise, the long-term 
benefits, enhanced trust, reduced risk exposure, and 
improved operational efficiency, significantly outweigh 
the initial costs.
Internal Audit: Enabling Strong Governance
The Internal Audit function plays a pivotal role in 
reinforcing good governance at GDIPLC. Through 
independent and objective evaluations, Internal Audit 
provides valuable assurance to the Board of Directors, 
the Audit Committee, and senior management 
regarding the effectiveness of the Company’s 
risk management processes and internal control 
environment.
In addition, Internal Audit acts as a catalyst in embedding 
a strong culture of risk awareness, compliance, and 
accountability throughout the organization.
Internal Audit and Compliance Activities at 
GDIPLC 
The Internal Audit & Compliance (IAC) Department 
of GDIPLC is responsible for ensuring the effective

improvement actions, are submitted to management 
and relevant governance bodies. Through rigorous 
assessments and continuous monitoring, the IAC

other applicable regulatory requirements, and all 
GDIPLC policies and procedures.

Internal Control Systems: The Foundation of 
Sustainable Success
Internal control systems are not merely procedural 
requirements; they form the foundation upon which 
a resilient and high-performing organization is 
built. These systems guide the organization toward 
achieving its strategic objectives while managing risks 
and promoting operational efficiency.
At GDIPLC, we fully recognize the critical importance of 
strong internal controls and have adopted the globally 
recognized Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of 
the Treadway Commission (COSO) framework as the 
guiding structure for our internal control environment.
The COSO Framework: A Globally Recognized 
Control Model
The COSO framework defines internal control as a 
comprehensive and integrated process involving 
the collective efforts of the Board of Directors, 
management, and employees across all levels of the 
organization. The framework is designed to provide 
reasonable assurance regarding the achievement of 
organizational objectives in three key areas:
•	 Operations: Ensuring the effective and efficient 
conduct of business activities.
•	 Reporting: Safeguarding the reliability, accuracy, 
and integrity of financial and other critical 
information.
•	 Compliance: Ensuring adherence to applicable 
laws, regulations, policies, and ethical standards.
Continuous Monitoring and Oversight
The effectiveness of GDIPLC’s internal control system 
is reinforced through continuous monitoring and 
proactive oversight. This responsibility is shared across 
multiple governance layers:
•	 Board of Directors: Provides overall oversight 
and ensures the integrity and effectiveness of the 
internal control environment.
•	 Audit Committee: Independently reviews and 
evaluates the adequacy and effectiveness of 
internal controls, including financial reporting and 
risk management processes.
•	 Senior Management: Responsible for establishing, 
implementing, and continuously monitoring 
internal controls within their respective functional 
areas.
This multi-tiered governance approach enables 
the timely identification and remediation of control 
weaknesses, thereby safeguarding the Company’s 
assets, reputation, and long-term sustainability.

6.3.3 OVERSIGHT IN ACTION: ROLE OF

Independent Assurance through a Risk-Based 
Audit Approach
The Internal Audit function at GDIPLC operates as 
an independent and objective assurance mechanism, 
providing robust oversight over operational and 
financial processes across the organization. Acting 
as a critical governance safeguard, the Internal Audit 
team evaluates the effectiveness of risk management, 
internal controls, and governance practices.
Significant audit findings, together with insightful and 
actionable recommendations, are formally presented to 
the Audit Committee, enabling informed oversight and 
continuous improvement. GDIPLC adopts a risk-based 
internal audit methodology, ensuring audit resources are 
strategically aligned with areas of highest risk exposure. 
This approach provides the Audit Committee and senior 
management with reasonable assurance regarding 
the adequacy and effectiveness of the Company’s risk 
management and internal control framework.
Audit Scope, Execution, and Reporting 
Discipline
Internal audits at GDIPLC encompass a comprehensive 
review of processes, transactions, and systems across 
the enterprise. Audit engagements are conducted 
in accordance with a formally approved, risk-based 
annual audit plan.
Key audit observations, control deficiencies, and 
recommendations are reported to the Audit 
Committee on a quarterly basis. The Internal Audit 
team actively monitors management action plans and 
the implementation status of audit recommendations 
to ensure timely and effective remediation.
Integrated Compliance Framework and 
Oversight
GDIPLC maintains a robust compliance framework 
supported by comprehensive internal policies, procedures, 
and an employee Code of Conduct. This framework 
governs daily operations and reinforces adherence to the 
highest ethical, legal, and regulatory standards.
The Compliance function plays a vital role in:
•	 Disseminating regulatory updates, circulars, and 
guidelines issued by insurance regulators and 
other authorities
•	 Providing advisory support and guidance to 
employees on regulatory and compliance matters

Compliance function continuously assesses the 
adequacy and effectiveness of the compliance 
framework through an integrated risk-based audit plan. 
Significant compliance issues identified are reported 
to the Audit Committee, and corrective actions are 
closely monitored to ensure sustainable compliance.

Green Delta Insurance PLC commenced operations as 
a non-life insurer in 1996 and has since evolved into 
one of the most respected and trusted names in the 
Bangladeshi insurance industry. With a diversified 
portfolio designed to meet the needs of both individual 
and corporate clients, the Company combines 
innovative insurance solutions with a strong emphasis 
on customer service and technology-enabled delivery. 
Its nationwide presence, sustained performance, and 
extensive recognitions continue to reinforce its role as 
a key contributor to the development and resilience of 
Bangladesh’s insurance landscape.
Further details of the Company’s corporate profile are 
available on page 23 of the Annual Integrated Report 
2025 .
Mission and Vision of GDIPLC
As a responsible and forward-looking insurance 
institution, Green Delta Insurance PLC remains firmly 
committed to upholding its mission and vision across 
all aspects of its operations. These guiding principles 
shape strategic decision-making, operational conduct, 
and stakeholder engagement, ensuring that the 
Company continues to create long-term value while 
safeguarding the interests of society and the economy.
Details of the Mission and Vision are provided on the 
relevant page of this report.
Culture, Ethics, and Values
At Green Delta Insurance PLC, a strong culture of 
integrity, excellence, and collaboration forms the 
cornerstone of sustainable success. Ethical conduct 
and shared values guide every aspect of the Company’s 
operations, reinforcing trust, accountability, and 
professionalism across all levels of the organization. 
These principles are embedded in policies, practices, 
and daily conduct, supporting a resilient and values-
driven corporate culture.
Further information on culture, ethics, and values is 
available on page 173 of this report.
Ownership and Operating Structure
Green Delta Insurance PLC is incorporated as a public 
limited company under the Companies Act, 1994, 
and operates under the regulatory oversight of the 
Insurance Development and Regulatory Authority 
(IDRA) of Bangladesh. The Company is publicly 
listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE), ensuring 
transparency, accountability, and adherence to capital 
market regulations.
Its operations are primarily focused within Bangladesh, 
where it offers a comprehensive range of non-life 
insurance products and services to individuals, 
businesses, and institutions across diverse sectors of 
the economy.
Key Activities and Markets
The Company’s core activities and product offerings 
are governed by the Insurance Act, 2010, and the 
regulatory framework prescribed by IDRA. Green Delta 
Insurance PLC provides a broad spectrum of non-life 
insurance solutions encompassing property insurance, 
including coverage for fire, earthquake, flood, marine, 
and related risks; casualty insurance, such as motor, 
liability, and general casualty lines; personal insurance 
products including health and travel insurance; 
and engineering insurance covering construction, 
machinery breakdown, and allied risks.
Operating exclusively within the Bangladeshi market, 
Green Delta serves a wide and diverse client base, 
ranging from individual policyholders to large 
corporate and institutional clients.
Competitive Landscape and Market Positioning
Green Delta Insurance PLC operates within a highly 
competitive and evolving insurance environment. The 
industry is characterized by intense rivalry among insurers 
competing on product innovation, pricing, service quality, 
and distribution reach. Customers exercise significant 
bargaining power due to price sensitivity and the 
availability of alternative risk management options, while 
reinsurance partners and investment counterparties play 
a critical role in influencing underwriting capacity and 
financial performance. The potential entry of new market 
participants and the availability of substitute risk mitigation 
mechanisms further intensify competitive pressures.
Within this dynamic landscape, Green Delta Insurance 
differentiates itself through a strong and trusted brand, 
a customer-focused operating philosophy, innovative 
and inclusive product offerings, and a robust nationwide 
distribution network. These strengths, built steadily 
over four decades, continue to reinforce the Company’s 
leadership position and support its purpose of securing 
tomorrows for generations to come.

7.3 GOVERNANCE AT THE CORE: GUIDING 
PRINCIPLES AND LEADERSHIP 
Corporate governance defines the relationships 
between management, the Board of Directors, 
shareholders, and key stakeholders, providing a 
structured framework for setting objectives, executing 
strategy, and monitoring performance. Strong 
governance is fundamental to sustainable value 
creation and long-term resilience.
At Green Delta Insurance, we uphold the highest 
standards of corporate governance, recognizing its 
critical role in safeguarding trust and delivering enduring 
value. Through active stakeholder engagement, our 
governance framework ensures strategic alignment, 
robust risk oversight, accountability, and operational 
excellence.
We remain fully committed to international best 
practices and strict compliance with all applicable 
regulatory requirements, including the guidelines 
issued by the Insurance Development and Regulatory 
Authority (IDRA), the listing regulations of the Dhaka 
and Chittagong Stock Exchanges (DSE & CSE), and 
the Corporate Governance Code prescribed by the 
Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission 
(BSEC).
GDIPLC’s leadership framework reflects a diverse 
and highly skilled composition, encompassing 
a wide range of professional backgrounds, 
expertise, gender, and experience. Regulatory 
guidelines also inform the design of this 
governance structure, ensuring compliance while 
enabling effective oversight.
This report offers a detailed view of our leadership 
structure, highlighting the qualifications and 
experience of Board members. It also presents key 
indicators of Board composition and the workings of 
Board subcommittees. Collectively, these governance 
mechanisms drive value creation by steering and 
monitoring the company’s strategic direction.
Green Delta Insurance PLC: Leadership Structure 
– A Dynamic and Forward-Looking Approach
The governance of Green Delta Insurance PLC is 
guided by a dynamic and visionary Board of Directors, 
entrusted with steering the company’s strategic 
direction and ensuring sustainable, long-term success. 
The Board plays a central role in defining effective 
business strategies, establishing robust governance 
practices, and appointing highly qualified professionals 
to key subcommittees.
To protect the company’s reputation and 
manage unforeseen risks, critical functions such 
as risk management and internal audits operate 
independently from day-to-day business operations. 
This separation provides strong, impartial oversight 
and fosters a resilient control environment.
Green Delta’s governance framework is firmly anchored 
in a comprehensive regulatory landscape, including 
guidelines from IDRA circulars, the Companies Act 1994 
(as amended through 2020), Bangladesh Securities and 
Exchange Commission (BSEC) notifications, and the 
company’s own Memorandum and Articles of Association.
The Board is composed of a diverse and accomplished 
group of professionals, bringing expertise from 
multiple disciplines. This diversity of perspectives 
enhances the quality of decision-making and ensures a 
balanced, strategic approach to governance.

At Green Delta Insurance PLC, stakeholder 
stewardship has defined our journey for four decades. 
As we celebrate 40 Years of Securing Tomorrows, 
our commitment extends beyond underwriting risks 
,  it encompasses safeguarding long-term value for 
customers, shareholders, employees, regulators, 
partners, and communities.
Understanding and responding to stakeholder 
priorities is not a parallel process; it is integral to 
our strategy, governance architecture, and business 
model. Through a structured materiality framework 
and proactive engagement mechanisms, we ensure 
that stakeholder expectations meaningfully shape our 
decisions, performance, and future outlook.
Institutionalising Material Matters into 
Corporate Strategy
Strategic Integration of Material Issues
We adopt a disciplined materiality assessment process 
aligned with global sustainability and governance 
benchmarks. Key outcomes are directly embedded into:
•	 Corporate Strategy & Business Planning ,  Ensuring 
alignment between financial performance and 
ESG imperatives.
•	 Risk Management Framework ,  Integrating 
economic, regulatory, climate-related, and social 
risks into enterprise risk oversight.
•	 Capital & Resource Allocation ,  Prioritising 
investments that deliver sustainable and inclusive 
growth.
•	 Board & Committee Oversight ,  Material 
matters are periodically reviewed at the highest 
governance levels to ensure accountability and 
transparency.
This structured integration strengthens our resilience 
while reinforcing our long-term value creation 
philosophy.
Targeted, Impact-Driven Initiatives
In response to stakeholder priorities, we implement 
focused initiatives designed to generate measurable 
impact:
•	 Operational Excellence & Digital Transformation 
,  Enhancing service delivery, efficiency, and 
customer experience.
•	 Customer-Centric Product Innovation ,  
Expanding inclusive insurance solutions to bridge 
the protection gap.
•	 Climate & Environmental Responsiveness ,  
Integrating sustainability considerations into 
underwriting and investment decisions.
•	 Community & Financial Inclusion Programs ,  
Supporting underserved segments and advancing 
insurance penetration in Bangladesh.
•	 Human Capital Development ,  Investing in 
leadership, diversity, and professional capacity-
building.
Continuous review mechanisms ensure these initiatives 
remain relevant amid evolving market dynamics.
Performance Monitoring & Transparent 
Reporting
Accountability is central to our governance ethos. 
We:
•	 Track material KPIs through structured internal 
dashboards.
•	 Align disclosures with leading reporting practices 
and regulatory requirements.
•	 Communicate progress transparently through 
integrated and sustainability reporting frameworks.
This disciplined performance monitoring reinforces 
trust and strengthens stakeholder confidence.

This participatory approach ensures our strategic

7.5 LEVERAGING CAPITALS: FOUNDATIONS 
FOR SUSTAINABLE GROWTH
Green Delta’s capitals, including financial, manufactured, 
intellectual, human, social and relationship, and natural, 
represent dynamic resources whose value evolves in 
response to our activities and outcomes. In line with 
the <IR> framework, we recognize the interconnections 
among these capitals and their collective impact on value 
creation. Each capital is strategically aligned with our key 
pillars and material matters, with associated risks and 
mitigation measures carefully considered. This integrated 
approach underpins a holistic value creation model, 
delivering sustainable benefits to all our stakeholders 
over the short, medium, and long term.
Laying the Cornerstone for Sustainable Growth
At Green Delta, we are committed to cultivating 
a resilient and sustainable business that delivers 
enduring value to all stakeholders. Our strategy 
balances profitability with innovation, seizing emerging 
market opportunities while maintaining disciplined risk 
management. A testament to this prudent approach is 
our robust solvency ratio, which stood at 2.4 times as 
of  December 31, 2025, underscoring our dedication to 
long-term stability and balanced growth.
FINANCIAL CAPITAL: FINANCIAL STRENGTH 
AND RESILIENCE
Financial Capital: Driving Sustainable Growth
Green Delta’s financial capital, encompassing internal 
accruals, borrowings, and shareholders’ equity, underpins 
our growth strategy. We remain committed to sustainable 
expansion while preserving a strong and resilient balance 
sheet. As of December 31, 2025, shareholders’ net worth 
stood at BDT  7,186 million. Our “AAA” credit rating from 
CRAB further affirms our financial stability, reinforcing 
confidence and trust among investors, policyholders, and 
other stakeholders.
Navigating Challenges
Green Delta remains vigilant to the effects of global 
economic dynamics, including inflationary pressures, 
rising interest rates, and currency fluctuations. To 
safeguard our financial resilience, we have implemented 
robust solvency and liquidity management strategies, 
ensuring stability even in uncertain economic 
conditions.
Looking Ahead
As we chart our path forward, we remain focused on 
enhancing operational efficiency and adapting to an 
evolving regulatory environment. We will continue to 
seize strategic growth opportunities, particularly in the 
bancassurance segment, while maintaining operational 
resilience across all business lines. Having successfully 
navigated recent nationwide challenges, Green Delta is 
strategically positioned to drive sustainable growth and 
deliver long-term value to all stakeholders.
Manufactured Capital: Expanding Reach and 
Accessibility 
At Green Delta, we adopt a flexible and inclusive 
approach to reaching our customers. Alongside digital 
platforms such as the InsuMama app that serve digitally 
inclined customers, we maintain a strong physical 
footprint through 30 branches nationwide and an 
extensive agent network. This omnichannel model 
ensures consistent and seamless customer experiences 
across diverse segments and geographies.
Our distribution strategy is anchored in diversification 
and customer-centricity. We continue to expand 
into semi-urban and rural markets, offering targeted 
solutions such as micro-insurance, agriculture 
insurance, and MSME insurance to address the specific 
protection needs of these communities.
In 2025, our branch network served approximately 
8,300 customers per month, facilitated the sale of 
over 1lakh policies, and supported a portfolio of more 
than 50+ insurance products, reflecting both scale and 
accessibility.
Bancassurance remains a critical growth lever. 
Through strategic partnerships with leading banks, 
we leverage established customer bases to deliver 
integrated financial solutions under one platform. 
These collaborations enhance customer convenience, 
strengthen our distribution capabilities, and advance 
our vision of making insurance accessible to all.
Intellectual Capital: Pioneering an Integrated 
Insurance Model
Technology and innovation form the foundation of 
our intellectual capital. Through advanced digital 
platforms, we empower customers, partners, and 
employees, strengthening our InsurTech capabilities 
and reinforcing our competitive edge. By actively 
embracing digital ecosystems and emerging 
technologies, we continue to introduce innovative 
solutions that redefine insurance delivery.

operations.

advancing digital processes.

and standards, we support the transition to a low-carbon 
economy and reinforce our commitment to responsible 
and sustainable business practices.

7.6 OUR BUSINESS MODEL: DRIVING VALUE

An organization’s business model outlines how it 
transforms inputs into outputs and outcomes through 
its core business activities, with the objective of 
achieving its strategic goals and creating sustainable 
value over the short, medium, and long term.
A detailed explanation of the Company’s business 
model is provided on page 281 of the Annual Report 
2025.
At Green Delta Insurance, we focus on efficiently 
transforming inputs into meaningful outputs and 
outcomes that deliver value to our customers and 
stakeholders. By minimizing trade-offs and optimizing 
operational efficiency, we ensure that resources are 
utilized effectively across the organization. During the 
year under review, our business activities consistently 
translated inputs into tangible stakeholder value, 
reflecting the continuous strengthening of our value 
creation model.
Green Delta Insurance PLC.’s business model 
articulates how the Company creates and sustains 
value for customers, shareholders, and society at large. 
It describes the structured process through which 
inputs are converted into outputs and outcomes, 
enabling the achievement of strategic objectives over 
the short, medium, and long term.

7.16 UNDERSTANDING THE ECONOMIC 
CONTEXT: GLOBAL AND LOCAL OUTLOOK  
Global Economic Outlook 2025: Navigating a 
Complex Landscape
The global economy is projected to continue its 
growth trajectory in 2026, albeit at a moderated pace. 
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) forecasts global 
economic expansion that reflects a steady yet cautious 
recovery from the lingering effects of the pandemic, the 
ongoing conflict in Ukraine, and persistent inflationary 
pressures.
While growth is expected to persist, it will likely be 
uneven across regions and sectors, underscoring the 
importance of resilience and adaptability in financial 
planning and risk management. Inflation, although 
projected to moderate from the elevated levels of 
2022, is expected to remain above target in several 
economies, presenting ongoing challenges for central 
banks and policymakers. The path to price stability is 
anticipated to be gradual, requiring careful calibration 
of monetary and fiscal policies.
A clear divergence in growth patterns is evident across 
the global economic landscape. Advanced economies, 
including the United States, the Euro area, and Japan, 
are projected to experience tepid growth, reflecting 
structural constraints and demographic pressures. 
In contrast, many emerging markets are expected to 
register stronger expansion, driven by robust domestic 
demand, favorable demographics, and sectoral 
opportunities.
The year ahead will not be without challenges. Slowing 
global growth may strain financial stability, particularly 
in the banking and insurance sectors. Geopolitical 
tensions and ongoing supply chain disruptions 
continue to create uncertainty, while the increasing 
frequency and severity of climate-related events pose 
material economic risks, from disruptions in agricultural 
production to infrastructure damage and migration 
pressures.
In this complex environment, forward-looking 
institutions are called upon to navigate uncertainty with 
prudence, innovation, and resilience. At Green Delta 
Insurance, our 40-year legacy of ‘Securing Tomorrows’ 
positions us to respond proactively to these dynamics, 
leveraging risk management, digital transformation, 
and sustainable practices to protect stakeholders, 
capture opportunities, and contribute to a stable and 
inclusive economic future.

7.18 STRATEGIC FOCUS: KEY INITIATIVES FOR

Driving Performance Through People, Technology, and Innovation
Green Delta Insurance PLC enhances its performance through a multi-pronged strategy that combines capacity 
building, operational efficiency, and stakeholder engagement. By investing in employee skills, knowledge, and 
productivity, we strengthen service delivery and foster organizational effectiveness. Our focus on customer 
satisfaction, public relations, and proactive engagement ensures that we consistently meet the evolving expectations 
of all stakeholders. Recognizing that a motivated, healthy, and engaged workforce is pivotal to productivity, we 
prioritize employee well-being, morale, and professional growth as central drivers of sustainable organizational 
success.
Navigating a Dynamic Insurance Landscape 
The insurance industry today stands at a pivotal crossroads. To thrive in a rapidly evolving and 
increasingly digital market, GDIPLC has identified three strategic imperatives to guide its growth and 
innovation: Digitality, Agility, and Versatility.
Digitality: Embracing the Future of Insurance 
Digital transformation is no longer optional, it is essential. GDIPLC is modernizing operations by 
embedding digital technologies into core processes, infrastructure, and product offerings. Leveraging 
big data analytics, machine learning, and automation, we streamline operations, optimize risk 
management, and enhance the overall customer experience. Simultaneously, our product suite is 
evolving to meet the unique needs of digitally-driven clients, ensuring relevance and competitiveness 
in an increasingly tech-enabled market.
Agility: Adapting and Innovating in Real Time 
In an environment defined by rapid technological disruption and changing customer expectations, 
agility is critical. GDIPLC fosters a nimble business model capable of anticipating market shifts, seizing 
emerging opportunities, and adapting to unforeseen challenges. By innovating products and services 
that address market gaps and deliver new value, we remain responsive to the evolving demands of 
retail and corporate clients, shareholders, and the broader community. This adaptability strengthens 
resilience and drives long-term, sustainable growth.
Versatility: Understanding People, Building Relationships 
At the heart of insurance lies a deep understanding of human behavior and risk perception. GDIPLC 
leverages data-driven insights to educate clients, encourage proactive risk management, and design 
effective solutions. Our versatile business model combines a robust omnichannel delivery network 
with a dynamic partner ecosystem, offering diverse services while maintaining strong direct customer 
relationships. This integrated approach ensures we can meet the varied and evolving needs of our 
clients while navigating the complexities of the modern insurance landscape.
Securing Tomorrows, Today
By uniting digital innovation, agile execution, and versatile service delivery, GDIPLC positions itself for 
continued success in an evolving market. As we celebrate 40 years of Securing Tomorrows, our strategy 
underscores a commitment to resilient growth, superior customer experiences, and sustainable value 
creation for all stakeholders.

MANUFACTURED CAPITAL: EXPANDING REACH & ACCESSIBILITY
Our manufactured capital comprises the full spectrum 
of physical and digital infrastructure that supports our 
integrated business model. It includes our nationwide 
branch network, advanced digital platforms, resilient 
IT architecture, and efficient operational processes, 
each designed to deliver seamless, reliable, and high-
quality service to our customers.
This foundational capital enables meaningful customer 
engagement, strengthens our presence within 
communities, and reinforces our responsibility as a 
trusted corporate citizen, supporting sustainable value 
creation today and into the future.
Customer-Centricity: Serving Diverse Needs 
with Agility
At Green Delta Insurance, we recognize that securing 
the future requires constant adaptability and a deep 
understanding of evolving customer expectations. Our 
customers span diverse demographics, preferences, 
and access points, and we respond with a thoughtfully 
designed omnichannel approach. While our digital 
platforms serve customers who value speed and 
convenience, our strong physical footprint, anchored 
by branches and affiliated agents, ensures personal 
engagement and trust. This integrated model delivers 
a seamless and consistent experience, enabling 
customers to connect with us through the channels 
that best suit their needs.
Expanding Our Reach through a Diversified 
Distribution Strategy
A diversified distribution mix is central to our growth 
strategy and long-term value creation. We continue 
to broaden our market presence through need-
based selling, ensuring sustainable and inclusive 
revenue growth. Technology plays a pivotal role in this 
effort, with platforms such as our InsuMama mobile 
application providing easy, on-demand access to 
products and services. At the same time, our extensive 
physical network of 30 branches across Bangladesh, 
supported by a strong agent force, ensures accessibility 
and proximity to customers nationwide.
Looking ahead, we are strategically expanding into 
semi-urban and rural markets, where demand for 
tailored protection solutions is growing. Through 
products such as micro-insurance, agricultural 
insurance, and MSME coverage, we address the

8.2 LEADING WITH PURPOSE: MESSAGE 
FROM THE MANAGING DIRECTOR & CEO 
ON SUSTAINABILITY
40 Years of Securing Tomorrows ,  Leading 
with Purpose, Sustaining with Responsibility
As Bangladesh continues its impressive economic 
ascent, it faces a defining paradox: accelerating growth 
alongside rising environmental vulnerability. Climate 
change, carbon pressures, and socio-economic 
disparities demand a new kind of leadership ,  one that 
balances ambition with accountability.
As we commemorate 40 Years of Securing Tomorrows, 
Green Delta Insurance PLC reaffirms that sustainability 
is not a parallel commitment ,  it is central to our 
strategic direction. Our responsibility as an insurer 
extends beyond financial protection; it encompasses 
safeguarding communities, strengthening resilience, 
and contributing to long-term national progress.
Climate Conscious Governance in a Risk-Driven 
Era
The Paris Agreement remains the cornerstone of global 
climate cooperation in 2025, marking a decade since 
its adoption and continuing to guide nations toward 
limiting global warming to well below 2°C, while pursuing 
efforts to restrict it to 1.5°C. Through mechanisms 
such as updated Nationally Determined Contributions 
(NDCs) and the Global Stocktake process, countries are 
reassessing ambition and accountability. Yet, scientific 
assessments consistently indicate that current progress 
remains insufficient to meet these targets without 
accelerated and collective action.
For Bangladesh ,  one of the world’s most climate-
vulnerable nations ,  the implications are profound. 
Rising sea levels, intensified cyclones, prolonged 
heatwaves, flooding, and ecological stress 
present systemic risks to livelihoods, food security, 
infrastructure, and overall economic stability.
At Green Delta Insurance PLC, we recognize that 
climate risk is financial risk. We remain committed to 
aligning our long-term governance, risk management, 
and innovation strategies with climate-resilient 
pathways ,  ensuring that economic advancement and 
environmental responsibility progress together.
Sustainability & Risk Management Embedding 
Environmental Discipline into Operations
Environmental stewardship begins with operational 
accountability. We continue to optimize resource 
usage and minimize environmental impact through 
structured internal initiatives:
•	 Promoting the use of both sides of paper
•	 Expanding recycling practices
•	 Limiting color printing and encouraging 
draft-mode printing
•	 Adjusting thermostat settings for energy 
efficiency
•	 Turning off lights and unplugging idle 
devices
•	 Prioritizing energy-efficient laptops
•	 Digitizing approval workflows to reduce 
paper dependency
•	 Embedding green practices into everyday 
processes
These measures contribute to reducing our carbon 
footprint while strengthening operational efficiency.
Digital Transformation as a Sustainability 
Enabler Innovation that Expands Access and 
Reduces Impact
The acceleration of digital adoption in Bangladesh, 
particularly following the COVID-19 pandemic, has 
transformed service delivery expectations. Green Delta 
Insurance has embraced this shift as both a customer 
service enhancement and a sustainability strategy.
Key milestones include:
•	 Launch of ‘Insu Mama’, enabling customers to 
purchase insurance policies digitally.
•	 Successful deployment of our full-phase 
AI-powered non-voice customer service 
platform, allowing customers to:
o Access product information
o Submit and track complaints or 
service requests
o View policy and insurance details in 
real time
This intelligent automation platform, supported by 
robust API integration developed by our IT team, 
enhances customer convenience while reducing 
physical paperwork, branch visits, and resource 
consumption.
Innovation, therefore, serves both service excellence 
and environmental responsibility.

8.3 OUR APPROACH: UNDERSTANDING 
SUSTAINABILITY REPORTING AT GREEN DELTA
40 Years of Securing Tomorrows ,  Reporting 
with Responsibility, Leading with Transparency
As Green Delta Insurance PLC commemorates 40 Years 
of Securing Tomorrows, sustainability reporting remains 
a cornerstone of our corporate accountability and 
long-term value creation strategy. For us, sustainability 
reporting is not a compliance-driven disclosure 
exercise; it is a structured reflection of how we 
manage environmental, social, and governance (ESG) 
responsibilities in a rapidly evolving risk landscape.
Through transparent and comprehensive reporting, 
we communicate our sustainability performance 
to stakeholders, reinforcing trust, credibility, and 
responsible stewardship.
Scope of Sustainability Reporting
A Holistic ESG Framework
Our sustainability reporting framework encompasses a 
broad and integrated set of ESG dimensions, ensuring 
that material risks and opportunities are appropriately 
identified, measured, and disclosed.
Environmental Responsibility
We report on our environmental footprint and resource 
management practices, including:
•	 Greenhouse gas emissions and climate-
related considerations
•	 Energy consumption and efficiency initiatives
•	 Water usage and conservation practices
•	 Waste management and recycling initiatives
•	 Biodiversity awareness and environmental 
protection measures
These disclosures reflect our commitment to mitigating 
environmental impact and promoting operational 
efficiency.
Social Commitment
Our social reporting focuses on the well-being of 
employees, customers, and communities, including:
•	 Employee engagement, development, and 
workplace practices
•	 Human rights adherence and inclusivity
•	 Community investment and outreach initiatives
•	 Health and safety standards
•	 Customer satisfaction and service excellence
Through structured social disclosures, we demonstrate 
how we create shared value for society.
Governance Integrity
Strong governance underpins sustainable performance. 
Our governance reporting covers:
•	 Corporate governance structures and 
oversight mechanisms
•	 Ethical conduct frameworks and compliance 
policies
•	 Anti-corruption and anti-bribery measures
•	 Stakeholder engagement processes
These elements collectively ensure accountability, 
transparency, and institutional integrity.
Strengthening Credibility Through 
Independent Assurance
Third-Party Verification and Impact Assessment
To enhance the reliability and transparency of our 
sustainability disclosures, Green Delta Insurance 
engages independent third-party assurance providers. 
This external verification process strengthens 
stakeholder confidence in the accuracy, completeness, 
and credibility of the reported information.
As part of the assurance engagement, the independent 
provider conducts an impact assessment covering:
•	 Materiality Assessment: Identification 
and prioritization of the most significant 
ESG issues relevant to Green Delta and its 
stakeholders.
•	 Data Verification: Validation of sustainability 
data to ensure accuracy and consistency.
•	 Process Evaluation: Review of internal 
controls, governance mechanisms, and 
sustainability management systems.
•	 Stakeholder Engagement Review: Evaluation 
of how effectively we engage stakeholders on 
sustainability matters.
This structured approach reinforces our commitment 
to transparent and high-quality reporting.
Safeguarding Objectivity
Statement of Independence
The appointed assurance provider operates under strict 
independence requirements to maintain objectivity 
and impartiality throughout the engagement process.

GREEN DELTA INSURANCE PLC

8.5 CARING FOR THE ENVIRONMENT:  
ECO-FRIENDLY PROGRAMS AND PRACTICES 
40 Years of Securing Tomorrows ,  Strengthening 
Environmental Stewardship
As Green Delta Insurance PLC marks four decades of 
sustained service to communities and stakeholders, our 
commitment to environmental stewardship remains 
steadfast. Caring for the environment is an integral 
component of our sustainability strategy, reflecting our 
belief that economic progress must harmonize with 
ecological responsibility. Our eco-friendly programs 
and practices seek to minimize our environmental 
footprint, enhance community resilience, and support 
long-term sustainable development in Bangladesh’s 
climate-sensitive context.
Leading the Way in Sustainability: The 3Rs in Action
Green Delta recognizes that sustainable practices 
are no longer optional, they are essential. With 
environmental stewardship embedded in its core 
operations, the company leads the charge by 
embracing the 3Rs: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. 
From actively reducing energy consumption and 
minimizing waste to promoting eco-friendly materials 
across all operations, Green Delta strives to minimize 
its environmental footprint. These efforts not only 
protect the planet but also serve as an inspiration, 
guiding other organizations toward sustainable 
practices.
Carbon Reduction and Operational Efficiency
While the services sector generally accounts for 
a relatively lower carbon footprint compared to 
industrial sectors, Green Delta Insurance is committed 
to continually reducing our environmental impact 
across our operations and stakeholder ecosystem. 
We explore and implement energy-efficient practices 
within our offices ,  such as optimized energy use, 
reduced paper consumption, and digitized workflows 
,  to drive carbon reduction internally and influence 
our supply chain to adopt greener practices. These 
efforts are designed not only to lower emissions but 
also to promote resource efficiency and organizational 
resilience.
Product Innovation for Climate Resilience
Recognizing the increasing threat of climate change to 
communities and economic activity, we are dedicated 
to fostering climate-resilient product innovation. Our 
approach involves developing insurance solutions 
tailored to the emerging climate risks faced by 
individuals and businesses. For example, we have 
already introduced agricultural insurance products 
that assist farmers in managing risks associated 
with flooding and extreme weather events, thereby 
strengthening rural resilience and supporting climate-
adaptive livelihoods. This product focus aligns with 
broader national efforts to enhance climate resilience 
and sustainable growth within vulnerable sectors.
Community Engagement and Environmental 
Education
Green Delta Insurance actively engages with 
communities to raise environmental awareness 
and promote sustainable practices. We regularly 
conduct sustainability outreach programs to educate 
stakeholders about environmental challenges and the 
importance of proactive management. These initiatives 
also facilitate deeper public understanding of the 
role of insurance in building resilience, strengthening 
financial inclusion, and enhancing environmental 
consciousness across communities.
Employee Well-being and Workforce Diversity
Environmental responsibility is closely linked to our 
commitment to employee well-being and inclusive culture. 
We prioritize a positive and diverse workforce environment 
that encourages participation in eco-friendly initiatives 
,  from internal awareness campaigns to involvement in 
community conservation activities. Through ongoing 
training, development programs, and workplace wellness 
efforts, we reinforce the connection between sustainable 
practice and organizational well-being.
Collaboration with Stakeholders for Environmental 
Impact
Achieving environmental sustainability requires broad 
collaboration. Green Delta Insurance actively partners 
with government agencies, industry associations, and 
civil society to support conservation, climate resilience, 
and social welfare initiatives. These collaborations 
extend our impact, aligning company actions with 
national and international climate and environmental 
goals, such as Bangladesh’s ongoing climate financing 
and resilience planning efforts. 
Measurable Objectives and Sustainability Targets
To ensure accountability and continuous improvement, 
our environmental programs are underpinned by 
measurable objectives and targets. We monitor 
progress across key performance indicators such as 
energy use, paper consumption, waste reduction, and 
product uptake in climate-resilient insurance lines. 
By setting clear targets and tracking outcomes, we 
ensure our environmental stewardship contributes 
meaningfully to sustainable development outcomes.
Looking Ahead: Creating Sustainable Futures
Green Delta Insurance’s eco-friendly programs and 
practices reflect our unwavering commitment to 
sustainability and responsible business conduct. As 
Bangladesh intensifies its focus on climate resilience 
and green growth ,  underpinned by significant 
development financing and policy momentum ,  
we remain dedicated to supporting environmental 
protection, community empowerment, and long-
term economic sustainability. Through purposeful 
action, collaboration, and innovation, we continue to 
contribute to a cleaner, more resilient, and inclusive 
future for all ,  securing not just financial outcomes but 
ecological well-being for generations to come.

Digital Insurance in the Palm of Your Hand
At the heart of Green Delta’s digital strategy is its

• Online Policy Purchase: Buy coverage quickly and

• Claims & Service Management: Track requests

single platform.

empowerment.

Intelligence

evolution. This smart platform enables customers to: 
– Access Product Information Instantly 
– Submit and Track Complaints or Service Requests 
– View Policy and Insurance Details in Real Time
Underpinned by a powerful API integration built by 
the company’s IT specialists, this automation enhances 
customer convenience while significantly reducing physical

consumption. By doing so, innovation also advances 
environmental responsibility ,  showcasing how digital 
excellence and sustainability can go hand in hand.

8.8 ISO CERTIFICATION: COMMITMENT TO 
INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS
8.9 DISCLOSURE ON THIRD PARTY 
ASSURANCE REPORT
Green Delta Insurance PLC remains steadfast in its commitment to delivering excellence in all aspects of its 
operations. While the Bangladesh Government and the Insurance Development and Regulatory Authority (IDRA) 
have not yet mandated ISO certification for the General Insurance sector, the company recognizes the value of 
internationally recognized standards in driving operational efficiency, quality, and customer satisfaction.
ISO (International Organization for Standardization) certification represents a benchmark of globally accepted best 
practices in quality management systems. Although not compulsory for the sector in Bangladesh, Green Delta 
Insurance PLC continuously aligns its processes with such international standards, ensuring robust governance, 
operational integrity, and exceptional service delivery.
Through ongoing process reviews, adherence to industry best practices, and a culture of continuous improvement, 
the company remains dedicated to providing reliable, efficient, and high-quality insurance services to its customers. 
This proactive approach underscores Green Delta Insurance PLC’s unwavering commitment to excellence, even 
beyond regulatory requirements, reinforcing its position as a trusted leader in the insurance industry.
Transparency is central to Green Delta Insurance PLC’s commitment to sustainable business practices. To uphold 
this, the company engages independent third-party assurance services to evaluate its environmental initiatives 
and impacts. These assurance reports provide detailed assessments of GDIPLC’s compliance with sustainability 
standards and regulations. The company also issues a Statement of Independence to ensure the impartiality and 
credibility of its assessors, reinforcing trust in its sustainability efforts and environmental disclosures.

9.1 CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY: 
CREATING SHARED IMPACT
Disclosure on CSR Activities done by GDIPLC and community welfare. 
Green Delta Insurance has always been an active patron of women and youth empowerment, social progress and 
development. Besides contributing to women and youth development, Green Delta Insurance has always been very 
supportive an organization towards the deprived and struggling community of the society. At Green Delta Insurance, we 
earnestly believe that it’s the responsibility of the privileged to help the deprived community of the society in order to 
help them get a better life. As reflection to that belief, Green Delta Insurance Company actively takes part in social causes 
that involve culture, heritage, women empowerment, child education, youth development, welfare of especially-abled 
or deprived children etc. Some of the notable and regular CSR activities of Green Delta Insurance Company Ltd. are as 
follows:
 • Child Education through Jaago Foundation: Green Delta Insurance sponsors a class of 40 kids studying at Jaago 
Foundation schools, who are now known as Green Delta Kids. Green Delta Insurance doesn’t only provide for 
their education, but also for their school dress, stationeries, textbooks etc. Green Delta will be continuing the 
sponsorship of those 40 kids up to their SSC graduation.
 • Donation to Libraries, Hospitals and for Social Causes: As part of giving back to society, Green Delta 
Insurance has always funded different social causes including donation to different libraries, hospitals, different 
foundations working for social causes and welfare.
Particulars of tree plantation and forestation
 • Tree Plantation: Green Delta Insurance is committed to maintaining the balance of the environment and protecting 
the environment from the harmful effects of climate change. Therefore tree plantation or afforestation has been 
adopted as one of the core CSR activities of the company. Green Delta undertakes its tree plantation drive through 
the farmer network of Green Delta who are beneficiaries of the crop insurance services as well as through third party 
partners, e.g. Give Bangladesh Foundation.

7. Risk disclosures
Financial risks management:
The Company has exposures to the following risks 
from its use of financial instruments:
•	 Credit risk
•	 Liquidity risk
•	 Market risk
Risk management framework
The Company’s board of directors has overall 
responsibility for the establishment and oversight 
of the Company’s risk management framework. 
The Company’s risk management policies are 
established to identify and analyze the risks faced 
by the Company, to set appropriate risk limits and 
controls, and to monitor risks and adherence to limits. 
Risk management policies, procedures and systems 
are reviewed regularly to reflect changes in market 
conditions and the Company’s activities. The Board 
oversees how management monitors compliance with 
risk management policies and procedures, and reviews 
the adequacy of the risk management framework in 
relation to risks faced by the Company
I. Credit risk
Credit risk is the risk of financial loss to the Company 
if a customer or counterparty to a financial instrument 
fails to meet its contractual obligations, and arises 
principally from the Company’s receivable from 
customers. The maximum exposure to credit risk is 
represented by the carrying amount of each financial 
asset in the statement of financial position.
II. Liquidity risk
Liquidity risk is the risk that the Company will encounter 
difficulty in meeting the obligations associated with its 
financial liabilities that are settled by delivering cash 
or other financial assets. The Company’s approach 
to managing liquidity is to ensure, as far as possible, 
that it will always have sufficient liquidity to meet its 
liabilities when due, under both normal and stressed 
conditions, without incurring unacceptable losses or 
risking damage to the Company’s reputation. Typically, 
the Company ensures that it has sufficient cash and cash 
equivalents to meet expected operational expenses, 
including financial obligations through preparation of 
the cash flow forecast, based on time line of payment 
of financial obligations and accordingly arrange for 
sufficient liquidity/fund to make the expected payments 
within due dates. Moreover, the Company has short 
term credit facilities with bank to ensure payment of 
obligation in the event that there is insufficient cash 
to make the required payment. The requirement is 
determined in advance through cash flow projections 
and credit lines with bank is negotiated accordingly.
III. Market risk
Market risk is the risk that any changes in market 
prices, such as foreign exchange rates and interest 
rates will affect the Company’s income or the value 
of its holdings of financial instruments. The objective 
of market risk management is to manage and control 
market risk exposures within acceptable parameters 
while optimizing the return.
a. Currency risk/foreign exchange rate risk
The Company is exposed to currency risk on purchases 
with foreign suppliers and borrowings. The Company’s 
foreign currency transactions are denominated in 
United State Dollar (USD). But the Company had no 
foreign currency denominated assets/liabilities as at 
reporting date.
